purpose: Record of every audio tour segment rendered: spoken text, hashes, duration and request id. Keys are published write-once under audio/.

entries.spokenText: A head drawn as a box. This is where the Faces begin, on October 26, 2021, with a white square head on green, two starburst eyes in boxes and a grid of block teeth. Twenty-seven works hang here, nearly all from the five weeks that followed, and every one of them builds a face out of rectangles.

The box is a frame for parts. Eyes go in as rings, spirals or targets, one in each square. The mouth is a second box with teeth set in it like a grille. A nose is a triangle or a bar. Around the parts the box is filled with scribble, hatching or stripes until it is solid, and then the whole thing is set on a flat color.
Watch the boxes tilt. The first heads sit square. By December they lean, stack and turn, and by the following spring the box has become a tall stack with a mouth of giant bars.
Four works from the first five weeks, October 26 to November 27, 2021. The box head arrives, loosens, and tilts.

The first work in the series. A white box head on green, two eyes as cyan starbursts in square frames, a nose of two yellow bars, and a mouth drawn as a grid of white block teeth. A red zigzag runs along the top like a hairline, and green, yellow and brown lines loop around the whole head. Seventy-seven strokes. Everything the room does is already here: the box, the parts in boxes, the grid of teeth.
A head in red, green and black scribble with a mane of red marks, one box eye ringed in white, and a wide red mouth at the lower right, open on white teeth.
An angular head in red, blue and yellow line on lavender, with an X in one box eye and bars in the other, a triangle mouth with green zigzag teeth, and a crown of spikes.
A head tipped on its side inside a yellow frame, drawn as a dense weave of white, green, orange and magenta lines, with two round eyes and a wide mouth at the bottom.
November 30 and December 1, 2021, eight heads in two days. The parts settle: ringed eyes, triangle noses, boxed teeth.

Two square eyes side by side, each a red and white target in a box, a red zigzag at the right like a cheek, and below them a long box of white triangle teeth. Cyan hatching runs across the eyes in diagonals. The ground is white with black and green marks at the edges. It is the clearest stack of boxes in the room: eye, eye, mouth, nothing else.

A yellow box head on red with a row of white spikes along the top for hair, two ringed eyes with black pupils, a triangle nose, and a box of white teeth under it. Two white hands reach up at the sides, and two small feet stand at the bottom edge. Green, pink and blue hatching fills the box. Nothing else in the room took as many strokes: 801.
A box head of purple scribble on yellow, two square eyes with black pupils, a triangle nose, and a white slot of a mouth stitched with black lines.
A box head in profile on teal, wearing a top hat, with a grin of white teeth, drawn in yellow, green and red hatching.
A box head on brown with a spiral eye and a box eye, yellow ring earrings at both sides, and a row of white block teeth in a red box.
A box head on maroon with slanted brows and spiral eyes, a red mouth of white fangs, drawn in cyan, white and yellow over dense scribble.
A crowned box head in profile on white, facing right, drawn in red, yellow and black line, with a grin of white teeth.
December 1 to 6, 2021. Nine heads. The box leans, the jaw becomes a drawer, and the stack gets taller.
A box head on navy drawn in cyan and yellow line, two pink spiral eyes, and a mouth of white blocks in a red box.

A head on dark brown with two ringed eyes under a pointed brow, and below them a jaw drawn as a drawer: a long box of white triangle teeth, then a second box, then a third, stacked down to the bottom edge. The whole head is filled with green, orange and pink scribble. The jaw here is a stack of its own, the first in the room.
A head with spiral eyes, spiral cheeks and a white zigzag crown, a V nose and a mouth of white zigzag, drawn in pink, orange and green line on dark brown.
A tall box head on black, two green ring eyes under a pink brow, and an open box of a mouth, drawn in pink, magenta and white scribble.
A box head on olive with two pink spiral eyes, a long nose, and a wide white mouth with yellow zigzag inside, drawn in green and blue facets.
A head drawn like a sign: stacked rectangles outlined in yellow, spiral eyes in boxes, and a box of black zigzag teeth, on dark olive.

A head on blue flattened into bands, drawn in yellow, orange and white line: a band of slit eyes with teeth above them, a band of nose, a wide band of lips, and a chin. The box has become a stack of stripes. Set beside the first head in the room, the parts are the same, eyes, nose, teeth, but every one has been pressed flat and widened.
A patterned head on red with two spiral eyes, two rows of gappy white teeth, and yellow and green bars at the sides.
January to March 2022. Six heads, spaced weeks apart, in which the box becomes a tall stack and the teeth grow huge.
A head of stacked patterned planes, one eye a box with a slot and the other a triangle, a band of huge white teeth across the bottom, in blue, red and yellow.

A blocky head on plum, painted in gold and yellow with white scribble over it, two red spiral eyes staring out, and a mouth of clenched white teeth in a dark box. The head has weight: the brow and the cheeks are modelled in light and shadow, and the eyes sit in deep sockets. It is the one head in the room with shadow, and the spirals in its eyes are the room's spirals, drawn into a face that looks back.
A tall stack of a head on teal, two round white eyes at the top, a mouth of giant white bars in a brown box, drawn in black, brown and blue.
A head on blue with one huge black eye in a white ring, four red capsules for a nose, a grid of white teeth in a red box, and a yellow wavy edge down the right.

A box head with cat ears on teal, hatched in orange, black and yellow, with crossed eyes in boxes, a long nose, and a grin of white teeth in a red mouth. The last work in the room, from March 29, 2022, four months after the yellow box head with the spiky hair. The parts are the same: boxed eyes, a triangle nose, teeth in a box. The box has grown ears.

Look again at the first box head, white on green, with its grid of teeth, and then at the cat-eared box from March. One is a box with parts in it. The other is a box with parts in it and ears. Five months of drawing, and the idea held.

Faces found in a tangle. The works in this room are drawn as dense, many-colored scribble, and the face comes out of it: a person with glasses, a man in a hat, a girl in a cap, a screaming head in a halo of white. Twenty-one works, from the second drawing in the series on October 27, 2021, to April 2022.

The scribble is not fill. It is the drawing. Hair, cheeks, beards and backgrounds are all the same looping line in different colors, and the features are the places where the line gets dense or changes color. Glasses are two loops. A mouth is a red knot with white inside it.

Watch how the tangle thins. In the first weeks the whole square is scribble. In February two faces are painted with the tangle only on top. By March the scribble has become hatching, and the faces snarl.
Five works from October 27 to November 27, 2021. People with glasses and hats, and a face lost in magenta.

A face with rectangular glasses and a fanged grin, drawn entirely in scribble: yellow and red for the hair, green and blue for the cheeks, a red knot for the mouth with white teeth inside it. The glasses are two white loops joined by a bar. The second work in the series, from October 27, 2021. Where the first was a box, this is a person, and the way the line finds a likeness is the method of the whole room.
A face with round purple glasses and a small red mouth, its hair yellow and blue scribble, drawn in loops of every color on a pale ground.

A face in a storm of magenta line. Twenty-eight strokes make the whole drawing, but each stroke is long, looping across the square again and again, and the face is found where the line turns blue and green: two eyes, a nose, a closed mouth. The face does not stand out from the tangle. It is the tangle, looked at long enough.
A head on red with two square goggle eyes, a big grin of pointed white teeth, two ears, and orange spiky hair, drawn in green and blue scribble.

A screaming head in a halo of white bands. The face is green and teal scribble with two dark eyes, a nose and an open mouth with white teeth, and around it concentric bands of white and green run to the edges like ripples. The bands are the only calm thing in the picture. The series' first scream, from November 26, 2021.
November 27 to December 6, 2021. Eight heads in ten days: a man in a hat, a girl in a cap, white fur, blond scribble, confetti.
A grinning face in purple, orange and yellow scribble, with a brow of dense black loops and a small open mouth.
A man in a wide-brimmed hat, drawn in dark purple and yellow scribble so dense the face is almost solid, on a pale ground.
A spiky dark head on pink with X marks for eyes and a frown, drawn in green, brown and red scribble.

A girl in a yellow cap and round glasses, inside a frame of pink, yellow and cyan lines, her hair falling in pink and black scribble. The cap is drawn as a box of yellow loops with a brim. Her mouth is a small red mark. It is the only framed work in the room and the only one where the scribble is held inside an edge.

A grinning face covered in white fur, the hair and beard drawn in short white and lilac strokes standing out in every direction, with a wide grin of white teeth and small eyes. The ground is orange and yellow loops. The fur is the scribble turned into hair, and the grin is the widest in the room.
A head of blond scribble with two dark eyes and a mouth of white block teeth in a red box, on a ground of colored bands.
A head on maroon with big ears, two target eyes, and red lips drawn in white and yellow line over red scribble.

A face in confetti. Small dabs of orange, blue, pink and green cover the whole square, and a small face sits in the middle of them with two dark eyes and a red mouth. The dabs are not loops; each one is a short stroke, and there are more than a thousand of them. Its 1,020 recorded strokes are the most of any work in the Faces.
December 6, 2021 to April 2022. Seven heads, spaced weeks apart. The scribble turns to hatching and the mouths open.
A screaming egg of a head on brown, drawn in blue and cyan scribble, its mouth a wide open oval with white teeth, ten days after the scream in the halo.

A face on purple with long lashes, angry brows and a snarl, painted in yellow and brown with scribble over it. The eyes are white with green irises under thick black lashes. The mouth is open on a row of white teeth, the lip pulled up. Below the face the body is a dark mass of black and yellow hatching. The face is painted first and the scribble is drawn on top, a change from the earlier rooms where the scribble was the face.
A face on yellow with brown hair, blue eyes under dark lashes, and a snarl of white teeth, painted an hour after the purple one.
A profile on dark blue with closed eyes, the face in white and red scribble, the hair a mass of red and black loops.
A hatched head on orange with yellow X marks for eyes and a thin grin of white teeth, drawn in brown, green and black hatching.

A tall screaming face on pink and purple, its mouth open on two rows of white fangs, its eyes red rings, with a second face behind it at the right. The line is black and white with yellow and blue over it. A month after the snarl on purple, the mouth has opened all the way and the face has doubled.
A bearded face on orange with square glasses and a grimace of white teeth, the beard drawn in green and white hatching.

In the magenta storm the scribble is everything and the face is barely there. On the purple snarl the face is painted and the scribble only sits on top. The line did the same work in both. It just stopped being the whole picture.

Faces with weight. The twenty works in this room are painted, not outlined: the cheek catches light, the eye sits in a socket, the chin casts a shadow. They come in two runs. In the winter of 2022 a set of quiet portraits, pale and soft, drawn in loops over discs of color. In the spring a set of glossy sculpted heads on flat bright grounds, shining like polished wood.
The ground changes with the paint. The winter faces float in haze, with no edge between the face and the air. The spring heads stand on one color, teal, orange, cyan, and their edges are hard.
In the winter portraits the eyes look at you, or down, or away. In the spring heads they narrow, cross and hollow out, and the mouth starts to sneer.
December 2021 and January 2022. A pale head in orange light, a face on black, and two portraits in haze.

A pale head in a glow of orange and red, its eyes crooked, one higher than the other, its teeth hanging from the lower edge of the face like a row of keys. The head is drawn in white, green and pink loops over soft discs of color, and the light seems to come from behind it. It is the first painted face in the series, from December 6, 2021, and the one that sets the room's method: discs of soft color first, then loops of line.
A face on black with a white band across the brow like a cap, a thick mustache, and a mouth open on white teeth, painted in purple, orange and blue.

A ghostly face in pale grey and lilac, with two dark hollow eyes and a small mouth, drawn in thin loops over discs of white and pink. The hair is pale strokes falling at the sides. Nothing is outlined. The face is made only of where the discs are lighter and darker, and the line on top is thin and loose. It is the most densely drawn work in the room.
A woman with blue eyes and a small mouth, painted in olive and brown over soft discs, her hair loose at the sides, looking out.
January 26 to March 25, 2022. Eight faces in shadow: a bald man, a profile in loops, a lace collar, a hat and goggles, a man with his eyes closed.

A bald man's head in dark brown and gold, with green eyes that look off to one side, a straight nose and a closed mouth. The light falls from the left, so the brow and the near cheek are gold and the far side of the face sinks into dark. A thin orange line follows the eyes and the lips. It is the stillest face in the series, and the most like a person seen in a room.
A profile in loose white and black loops on cream, facing right, with an orange mouth and no teeth, forty-four strokes over soft discs of pink and lilac.
A dark head on white, tilted back with the chin raised, modelled in brown and black with red, green and white loops over it, its eyes narrowed.
A long-haired figure in olive with dark eyes and a white lace collar, the collar drawn as a net of white lines and dots.
A grey head in a hat with two huge pale eyes like goggles, a grin of white teeth, modelled in grey and purple.
A man with his eyes closed, painted in brown and grey with orange and white line, on a ground of grey stripes.
A dark face on magenta with a mop of pink and gold hair and a red X in one eye, outlined in thick white, its mouth a grid of small teeth.
April 13 to May 22, 2022. Eight heads that shine: sculpted in dark paint, lit from one side, on flat bright grounds.

A glossy dark head on violet with one yellow eye and a wide grin of white teeth, drawn in white and black line over paint that shines. A row of white teeth sits on top of the head like a crown. The nose is a long triangle. It is the first of the glossy heads, from April 13, 2022, and it casts a shadow on the violet, the first shadow in the room.
A glossy head on orange with narrowed eyes and a sneer, painted in brown, gold and black with scribble over the crown.
A glossy dark head on lavender with a yellow cross in one eye and a target in the other, a grin of white teeth, and fingers resting on top of the head.

A glossy dark mask on a ground of orange and pink stripes, with two swirl eyes, a long nose, a row of large white teeth and a border of yellow beads around the head. The paint is black with white and blue highlights, and the beads are small yellow circles drawn at even spacing. The stripes behind it run in waves. With 372 recorded strokes it is the most worked of the glossy heads.
A glossy green head in a hat with flowers on the brim, on olive, with small eyes and an open mouth.
A glossy face on cyan with crooked eyes, one high and one low, a row of white teeth, and a crown of yellow scribble for hair.

A glossy dark head on orange, lit by pale beams from the upper left, its mouth open on white teeth, one eye a white ring in shadow. The beams are soft wedges of pale yellow laid over the head. Five months after the pale head in the orange glow, the light is back, but now it falls on something solid and casts a shadow. The last work in the room, from May 22, 2022.

The pale head in the orange glow is lit from behind, and the face is barely solid. The dark head from May is lit by beams. In both, the light is the subject. In the first it dissolves the face. In the last it strikes it.

Skulls, hoods and heads coming out of the dark. The twenty works in this room share a ground of black or near-black, and what the drawing does is pull a face out of it: with a halo of ochre, a white line, a pair of lit eyes, a grille of teeth. They run from December 2021 to April 2022.

Two kinds of dark are here. In some works the black is a flat ground, and the head is drawn on it in line, as in the hooded skull with letters on its brow, made in twenty-six strokes. In others the black is paint, and the head is modelled out of it with highlights, as in the blue head with yellow slit eyes.
Watch the teeth. They are nearly the only white in most of these pictures, and they are what the eye finds first: a zipper, a grille, four fangs, a row of pegs hanging from a jaw.
Four works from December 4 to 6, 2021. A head in an ochre halo, a black head on white, a blue head lit from inside, and a face in a pink frame.

A head on black inside a halo of ochre, with two target eyes in yellow rings, a white zigzag along the brow, and a mouth of white teeth drawn like a zipper. Inside the head the fill is colored scribble, cyan, pink and yellow, with black line over it. The halo is the only soft thing in the picture, a band of brown that keeps the head from falling into the black. The series' first dark work.
A black head on a white ground, with one ringed eye and one boxed eye, a long nose, and a grille of grey teeth in a red mouth, its inside a tangle of colored scribble.

A dark blue head with two yellow slit eyes and a grin of white teeth, painted in blue and black with white highlights along the crown. The eyes glow in their sockets, and the light on the head comes from the upper left, picking out the brow and leaving the jaw in shadow. The grin curves up at the right. The only painted head in the room that shines, and the first.
A face in a frame of pink loops on dark red, with one eye a sun of orange rays and the other an arched box, and a grille of white teeth at the bottom.
January 21 to February 9, 2022. Seven works in three weeks: a ghost skull, a skull in white line, a tall head with starburst eyes, and four hooded figures.
A skull drawn in yellow and orange loops over a ground of vertical dark strokes, with two hollow eyes and a grille of white teeth, like a ghost in a curtain.
A face drawn in white and red line on dark red, with X marks in both eyes, spiky lashes, and a small mouth of fangs, in forty-seven strokes.

A tall head on dark teal with two starburst eyes under spiky lashes, a green cross for a nose, and a mouth of five white teeth in a box. The head is drawn in white, orange and cyan line over soft vertical strokes of blue and grey, so it seems to stand in rain. The two eyes are different: a white disc at the left, an orange ring at the right. The cross on the nose is drawn in green zigzag.

A black mass of hair on grey, and in it a face: two white eyes with dark pupils, a short line for a nose, and four white fangs. Twenty-three recorded strokes, the fewest in the room. The hair is drawn as a few loops of white line over black, and the black is one shape. The whole face is the eyes and the fangs.

A hooded skull on black, drawn in white line with a red hood, and the letters N N X Y Z written in red across its brow and its eyes. Two rows of white teeth sit below. Two hands rest at the bottom in red outline. Twenty-six strokes. The letters are the artist's name, and they sit on the skull where the eyes should be, so the name does the looking.
A hooded figure on black, its hood and shoulders outlined with yellow dots, a white face with one sun-burst eye and one red star eye, and a grille of white teeth in a red box.
A hooded head painted in orange and brown, with no face at all except a wide grin of white teeth in the dark of the hood.
February 12 to 21, 2022. A horned head, a skull with pink eyes lit by beams, a skull with blue eyes, and a bird skull.
A horned dark head on green, with two tall white eyes under a heavy brow and a grille of yellow teeth, drawn in black and blue scribble over soft green blobs.

A skull with two huge pink eyes, each a ring of magenta rays around a white center, lit by pale beams that cross the square from the upper left. The skull is drawn in black and colored line over dark, and the mouth is a row of white triangle teeth in a dark box. The beams are the first in the Faces, soft bands laid over everything. Where they fall, the lines show through them.

A skull painted in pink, brown and grey on black, with two blue eyes in dark sockets, each a ring of blue with a white highlight, and a row of white teeth hanging from the jaw at the lower right. Nothing is outlined. The skull is modelled in soft strokes with a thin white edge. Where the blue head of December glowed from inside, this one is lit from the front, and the eyes look wet.
A bird skull with a long beak, drawn in black, white, red and cyan strokes on dark brown, a brush of pale lines hanging from the jaw like a beard.
March 16 to April 25, 2022. Five heads: a box with an X eye, a chunky head with a heart for an eye, a head of blocks, a glossy bald head, and a skull with its jaw off.
A chunky head on dark grey with a red heart in a box for an eye, a box of white teeth, and two more boxes of teeth at the bottom like feet, in confetti scribble.
A head built from stacked blocks on dark navy, with one eye in a tilted box and the other a cluster of rings, a long bar of white teeth at the bottom.
A glossy bald head on black, its skin a weave of colored scribble, two ringed eyes, and a mouth open on white teeth, one eye at the right lit white.

A glossy skull on pink with spiky hair, one huge yellow eye, and its jaw come off, lying below the teeth as a separate row. The skull is painted in gold and black with white highlights, and the teeth hang from the upper jaw in a row of long pegs. Two months after the skull with blue eyes, the modelled skull is back, and this time it has come apart. The last work in the room, from April 25, 2022.

Look again at the hooded skull with the letters across its eyes, twenty-six strokes on black, and then at the glossy skull on pink with its jaw on the floor. One is nothing but line. The other is modelled, lit and broken. Both are skulls in the dark, and both make you look at the teeth.

Sparer faces on flat color. The twenty works in this room are drawn with less: a cartoon head in a few strokes, a mask of beads and petals, a diagram of a face in colored line with the ground showing through. Most are from the first four months of 2022.

The line does different things here. On some works it is a cartoon outline, thick and black, with a flat color inside. On others it is a diagram, drawing each part of the face as a shape and leaving the rest to the ground. And on one, the grey face with glasses, it is eight loops and nothing else.
The ground here is a color: lime, orange, yellow, teal, grey. In the earlier rooms it is filled or scribbled. Here the drawing sits on it like a sticker.
December 2021 to February 2022. A scribble mask on white, then a run of cartoon heads: goggle eyes on lime, a black head on red, a face with a peace sign.
An oval mask on white in cyan, pink and green scribble, with two eyes looking up, red lips, and a grin of white teeth, drawn on December 3, 2021.

A yellow-green face on lime, hatched in yellow and blue, with two goggle eyes in white boxes under a dark brow and a row of white teeth hanging from the chin. The face is a cartoon: a thick outline, a flat color, two boxes for eyes. The teeth hang below the jaw as a row of white pegs, like the pale head in the painted room, but drawn in line. The cartoon run begins here.

A grey mask inside a ring of yellow dots, with two white-dot eyes in dark boxes, a row of pink dots on the brow, and a mouth drawn as a grate of dark bars. Around the yellow dots, rings of grey scallops run to the edges like the rim of a shield. The mask is drawn in soft grey and teal with thin orange line, and it is the most ordered drawing in the room: every mark is a dot, a ring or a bar.
A black cartoon head on red, with two white eye boxes and small pupils, a red nose, a wide grin of white teeth, and white marks at the corners like motion lines.
A mask head on yellow filled with colored scribble, two white slots for eyes with red slits inside, and a grimace of white teeth in a red mouth.

A black head and shoulders on pink and purple, with a yellow X in one eye, an orange X in the other, small white fangs, and a black hand raised at the right in a peace sign. The figure is one flat black shape outlined in cyan, and the X marks are the only color on it. Seventy-four strokes. It is the one work in the room with a gesture.
February 19 to March 6, 2022. A skull with a crown for an eye, an owl, a gold blob with star eyes, a skull in profile, a sun of petals and beads, and an angular head in a haze.
A cartoon skull in white line under cyan rays, with a yellow crown in a box for one eye and a window of red grid for the other, a grille of white teeth and lime fingers at the side.
An owl head on orange with pointed ears, two green ringed eyes crossed with red, and a grille of white bars for a mouth, drawn in black, blue and yellow hatching.
A gold blob of a head curved like a banana on green diagonal stripes, with two red star eyes and a grin of white fangs.
A skull in profile on teal, drawn in white and black line, with a sunflower for an eye, a crest of yellow loops, and a grid of thin lines over the whole square.

A sun of a mask on dark green: a round face ringed with yellow petals, each with a dot, and a row of red spikes along the top like a crown. One eye is a white dot in a dark socket, the other a ring with a white center. The mouth is white teeth in a dark oval. Beads of blue, pink and yellow run around the face. With 347 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the room, and the only one with every part in its place.
An angular head on a neck, drawn in black, white and blue line over a haze of soft gold and brown discs, its face a few straight strokes.
March 24 to April 16, 2022. Seven faces drawn as diagrams, from eight grey loops to a machine of rings and teeth on teal.

A face in eight grey loops on grey: two circles for glasses, a curl for a nose, a spiral for a mouth, and a cluster of pink and orange bubbles for hair. Fifty-eight strokes, each one a quick mark, make the sparest drawing in the whole collection. Nothing is filled and nothing is scribbled. It is the sparest face in the Faces.
A head of dark red scribble on grey with two yellow ex eyes, a blue bar falling from the face like a tear, and an orange band across the top.

A flat face on yellow, striped in blue, green and orange, with two pink X marks for eyes, four small dots across the brow, and a thick white outline with rays. At the lower right a small red face on a stick looks on with its own ex eyes. The stripes run down the face and drip at the chin. The outline is drawn with short strokes standing out from it like a child's sun.
A face on navy drawn in blue, pink and yellow line: a ringed eye in a box, a box with an X, a yellow crest, and a long white zigzag of teeth across the lower face.
A face on olive in white, orange and blue line, with a ringed eye and a spiky eye, two rows of hanging teeth, and a chain of white teeth across the bottom.

A face on teal with two eyes like propellers in rings, a red ball for a nose, a bar of white teeth in a red box, and a crown of yellow and blue ovals. Everything is drawn in line, and every part is a separate shape: a ring, a box, a ball, a bar. Three weeks after the face in eight grey loops, this is the diagram with all its parts filled in. The last work in the room, from April 16, 2022.

Look again at the face in eight grey loops, and then at the face of propellers and teeth on teal. Both are line on a flat ground. One leaves almost everything out. The other draws every part and still leaves the ground showing. That is the range of this room.

Box heads with their eyes struck through. In this room the eye is an X, a red cross, a plus sign, or a letter, and the box head of the first room comes back with its eyes cancelled. Twenty-six works, from December 1, 2021 to March 18, 2022, and then the collection piece, number zero zero zero zero, made in July.

The cross is drawn many ways. A red X over a ring. A plus sign in a white box. Two red bars. And in a handful of works the eyes spell the artist's name: an X in one box, a Y in the next, a Z in the third. The letters N, N, X, Y and Z appear as eyes, as a brow, and on number 48 as the whole face.

Watch the mouth under the crossed eyes. It is almost always a grid of white block teeth in a box, and as the eyes get stranger the teeth stay the same. The room ends on the one work that puts every mark in the series into a single square.
December 1 to 6, 2021. Eight box heads, the first with green crosses in its eyes, the last with the artist's name written across the whole face.

A box head inside a white box frame on green, with two ringed eyes crossed by green plus signs, a V of red and white for a nose, and bands of yellow and red filling the face. Two small boxes with spirals sit at the sides like ears. It is the first crossed eye in the series, from December 1, 2021, drawn not as a cancellation but as a plus sign laid over a target.
A rounded box head on dark teal in cyan and red scribble, two red crosses in blue eye boxes, and a mouth of white triangle teeth.
A box head on white in magenta and yellow scribble, two orange crosses in white eye boxes, and white block teeth in a tilted box.
A block head on blue stripes with two orange ringed eyes crossed in white, and a mouth open on two rows of white teeth, upper and lower.
A horned owl mask on blue with a yellow zigzag crown, a white X in one eye and a dot in the other, and a grille of white teeth in a red box.

The artist's name as a face. The letters N and N sit at the top in white, X Y Z in a box below them, a plus sign in cyan beside them, and a cross in a ring at the right. Below, a row of white ovals for teeth and a second row of ovals under a yellow wave. On purple and blue with yellow bars. Nothing here is a nose or a cheek; the face is made entirely of the name and its marks.

A dark square with neon slashes of lime, red, pink and blue across it, a pink X in one eye and a heart in the other, and a brown drip running down the center of the face. The mouth is a pink bar at the bottom. Where the name was drawn as a face a few hours earlier, here the marks have been thrown at the square: the X is a slash, the slashes are the face, and the drip runs through all of it.
December 31 to February 8. Six heads over five weeks, with red crosses, plus signs and target eyes, and long fangs.
A box head with coils at the sides like springs, two triangle eyes with red crosses, a big grid of white teeth, drawn on the last day of 2021.

A box head on grey with two pink boxes for eyes, each with a white plus sign, a row of big white block teeth in a red box, and a comb of yellow and black spikes along the top for a crown. Drawn on the morning of January 1, 2022, in ninety-four strokes. A month after the first green crosses, the plus sign has become the whole eye: a white cross in a pink box, nothing else.
A head on yellow and white with a sunflower for one eye, green petals around a target, and a red cross for the other, two boxes of white teeth side by side.
A box head on dark brown with a red cross in one eye and a red X in the other, long white fangs in a dark mouth, and yellow wavy marks floating on the ground.
A box head on orange in pink and blue line, a red cross in one eye and a red X in the other, a grille of white teeth in a red box, and a crest of yellow strokes.
February 9 to 20, 2022. The eyes become letters. Six heads in which an X, a Y and a Z sit where the eyes should be.

A box head on lavender with three boxes in a row for eyes, and in them an X, a Y and a Z in red. Below, two boxes of white teeth side by side and a third box of teeth at the bottom. Horns of red line stand at the top corners. The name has moved from the brow to the eyes, one letter to a box, and the head has three eyes to hold it.
A box head on teal with a white X in one eye and a red cross in the other, a crown of yellow spikes, and a long bar of white teeth in a red box.
A round head on orange and purple with two star ex eyes in boxes, a white nose, and a ring of white teeth around the chin like a collar.
A head on magenta with a yellow X in one eye and a blue target in the other, a yellow Y for a nose, a grin of white teeth and a second small mouth under the left eye.

A box head on olive with three boxes for eyes in a row, X, Y and Z in red, a triangle for a nose like a house, a column of blue ovals, and a box of white teeth. Eleven days after the first three-eyed head, the letters are back in their boxes, and the head is built from blocks: a box for the eyes, a box for the nose, a box for the teeth.
A box head on orange with a yellow hat brim, two red X marks in white eye boxes, a bar of white teeth, standing on a post like a sign.
February 27 to March 18, 2022, five last box heads, and then the collection piece, drawn in July, which gathers every mark in the series into one square.
A box head on purple standing on two posts, with two eyes of red bars in boxes, a yellow crest, and a long bar of white teeth.
A box head on yellow with goggles, two white ovals joined by a bar, each with a red cross, and a wide grin of white teeth.

A box head on maroon with a red and white X in a cyan box for one eye and a slash in the other, orange horns, a long nose, and a grin of white teeth, the last of the crossed boxes, from March 18, 2022.

The collection piece, an edition of one, drawn on July 20, 2022, four months after the last numbered face. A dense square of pattern: the letters N, N, X, Y and Z drawn large in the center, a red heart at the top, a flower at the right, beads, zigzags, grids and teeth filling every corner. With 753 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the Faces. The name that was a face in December is here the whole picture.

The first crossed eyes were green plus signs on a box head in December. The last work is the collection piece, where the letters of the name fill the square. The X started as a mark on an eye. By July it was the subject.

For ten weeks in the spring of 2022 the same formula held: one flat color, one black shape, and a ring of short wavy lines. Twenty-eight works came out of it, from a snarling cat on March 25 to a cat the size of a hill on June 2. What each creature is, and what it is doing, comes through the outline alone.

Inside the black there is almost nothing. A pair of spiral eyes, or two small X marks, and sometimes a row of jagged teeth. A spiral makes a cat look dizzy or wild. An X closes an eye for good, and the same X on a rabbit, a bee and a whole crowd of heads runs through the room like a signature.

The wavy lines are the other constant. They sit in the color around the figure, never touching it, and they make a still black shape hum. Watch them when a black horizon arrives under the creatures, when the figures turn hairy, and when, in the last days, the black is nearly all that is left.
The room begins with four cats. The first arrives in March, the other three in one week of April, and between them they set every rule the next ten weeks will follow.

A black cat arches over a scribbled yellow and white ground, its back one long diagonal across the square. The eyes are two red spirals in orange boxes, and the mouth is a white zigzag of teeth. Thick yellow zigzags fill the teal around it. In every later work the ground is a flat black band, or nothing at all. Here it is scribbled in color.
The same cat lies on a black ledge with its tail up, and nothing is drawn inside it but two yellow spirals and two white fangs.

One day later the same cat lies on the same ledge, facing the other way. Its body is filled with yellow scribble, so the black shows only at the edges, and the cat turns from a cut-out into something furred. Red crossed eyes and a red stitch of a mouth are the only marks on the fur. It is the one work in the room where the black shape is opened up from inside.
Balanced on a black ball, a cat curls its tail over its head, with blue spiral eyes and a white saw-tooth grin.
Six works in three days, April 25 to 27. The cat gives way to other creatures, a black horizon appears under them, and two are set inside a frame.

Two cats sit facing each other on a red ground, and between them a heart made of two black bars meets at its point. Both have yellow spiral eyes and a jagged yellow grin. Yellow lines fill the red in loose rows that follow the two bodies. It is the only pair in the room.
Inside a white frame, a black bear hugs its round belly in the corner of a yellow square, with no wavy lines at all.
No horizon under this one. A black bird with one yellow spiral eye and a zigzag beak floats on teal.
After three weeks away, the black turns hairy. Scarecrows are drawn in bristling strokes, grass grows along the horizon, and the X mark arrives for the eyes.
On a single pole, a scarecrow holds its arms out, drawn in scratchy strokes, with grass bristling along the black horizon and every wavy line in black on orange.

The scarecrow again, a day later, now standing in a field with a black cat beside a purple fence. Its face has two round yellow eyes and its body is a mass of hatched strokes. Yellow wavy marks are everywhere, inside the fence as well as around the figures. It is the most densely drawn work in the room.
A rabbit sits upright on red with both ears straight up, its eyes two X marks and its mouth a small zigzag, a line down its chest like a seam.
Dancing on one leg, a round-headed figure bends its arms, ex eyes, the wavy lines black again on orange.

A witch in a pointed hat stirs a cauldron from a step ladder, and the cauldron says Scaffold eeth in scratchy pale letters. The witch is drawn like the scarecrows, in bristling strokes with one X for an eye. Black wavy lines fill the lime green. With 152 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the room, and the only one with words in it.
The last week of May brings the small things: a snail, a turtle, a bee, a balloon, a worm, a spider, a flower and a crowd. Each gets one shape, one color and its ring of lines.
Along the horizon crawls a snail with a yellow spiral shell and a tiny cat-like face.
Over the horizon a bee with ex eyes hovers, while a small black flower with spiral eyes looks up at it from the lower right.
On a long wavy string a balloon with spiral eyes and a jagged grin rises, and a black hand at the bottom corner lets it go.
Out of a bitten apple on a steep black slope rises a worm with ex eyes, the lines around it black on green.
From the top edge a spider hangs on a thin thread, legs tucked around a round body, three small yellow marks for a face.

A crowd of black heads fills the bottom of a yellow square, every face a pair of X marks. The yellow sits inside a thick black border, so the square is a window and the crowd stands at its sill. Not one of them has an open eye.

The room ends on June 1 and 2 with four works that take the formula in four directions: a figure drawn in scribble, a child reaching up, a page of tiny figures with no color at all, and one last enormous cat.
Bent over two crates marked with sunbursts, a scribbled figure rests its hands on the lids, while a small snail crosses the pink at the bottom left.

A figure seen from behind reaches up to a small black heart that gives off sparks. The face is turned away, and all that shows of it is one small X on the cheek. The wavy lines, black now, stand up along the figure's back like hair.
Rows of tiny black figures tumble across a white page, each one scribbled in a few strokes, with a single red one beside the signature.

A cat the size of a hill crouches on a black slope, filling the square from edge to edge, and looks out with yellow spiral eyes and a stitched grin. Its tail rises off the top of the picture and comes back down in a hook. Pale blue lines mark the legs and the curve of the back, the same blue that outlined the first cat in March. Where the first cat snarled, this one sits.

Go back to the first cat and the last. The one from March arches and bares its teeth on a scribbled ground. The one from June fills the whole square and sits still, with the same blue outline and the same spiral eyes. Between them the room tried the formula on twenty-six other creatures. Look again at the wavy lines around each one. They are what holds the room together.

In this room the eyes are lamps. Twenty-one works from May 2022 share one device: a head or a creature whose eyes give off light, and a beam that crosses the square like a searchlight. Where the light lands, the drawing goes pale and the lines show through it. Where it does not, the ground stays dense, scribbled in olive, red and blue.

The light takes two forms. In the framed heads it is a hard wedge, drawn as a solid band of pale yellow laid over everything, with a bright white disc where it starts. In the painted creatures, the bears and the hooded figure, it is a halo, soft at the edges, with round spots of glare floating in it like dust in a projector.

Twelve of the works came in five days, May 7 to 11. The rest arrived in a second run ten days later. Watch what the beam does to the thing it comes from: it fixes where you look, and it turns the rest of the head into shadow.
Six framed heads open the room, drawn between May 7 and 9. Each one is packed to the frame with marks, and each one is cut by a beam.

A head tips to the right inside a tan frame, two square eyes glowing white, and a beam spills out of them toward the lower right corner. The mouth is a panel of upright teeth, lit from the same source. Around the head the ground is a weave of olive, yellow and blue scribble, with orange fence posts along the bottom. The light is drawn as a pale band laid over all of it, so the scribble shows through the beam like a pattern through gauze.
Turned on its side, a machine of a head: a bar of four round dials, a stack of triangles, a grid for a cheek, and beams crossing the whole thing on the diagonal.
One huge round eye on the left throws a wide beam down and to the right, past a small square eye and a grinning row of teeth.

The same head again, under green light. The drawing is the one from number 75 with the colors shifted: the beam is lime, the eye has a spiral in it, and the whole ground has gone cool. Its title is the only one in the room with words, cash lightning. Set the two side by side and the difference is the light alone, warm on one and acid on the other, falling on identical lines.
Under a glass dome on a round base, a small creature with two glowing eyes sits in a flood of yellow rays, the whole picture lit from behind it.
Two days, May 9 to 11, and six works. A furry creature appears twice, once with its eyes lit and once in the dark, and then the heads put on helmets.
A round, furry creature with two enormous glowing eyes squats on a patch of grass, orange stripes behind its head, its paws folded over its belly.

The same creature, half an hour later, with the lights off. It sits in plain black now, inside a white border, and its eyes are two dark spirals where the lamps were. The fur is the same hatching, the paws are the same, the belly has the same pale patch. Without the glow the creature looks smaller and more worried, and the drawing is mostly shadow.
In profile, facing left, a head sends two beams out of two square eyes, while a black band on the right edge holds the picture like a shoulder.
A creature with a yellow beak and a row of hanging teeth like icicles, its eyes two glowing leaf shapes, set in a frame of pale blue.
A blue head with a crest like a helmet, a wide grin of white teeth, and a single beam from a square eye at the upper left.
Painted, not scribbled: a helmeted figure in gold and black holds its hands together under a grinning mouth, lit by a wide beam from the upper left.
After nine days away the glow comes back bigger. From May 20 to 22 the eyes become whole lamps, and two of the creatures start to speak.
A head with a mop of wild yellow and black hair, a thin neck, and two orbs of light for eyes, each one larger than the mouth beneath it.
A teddy bear with sparking antennae sits in a burst of orange rays, its eyes two small lamps and the word BULLISH written across its chest.
A head in white scribble over pink and orange, two beams driving to the right out of the eyes, three orange drips hanging from the top.
An armored figure in black and gold, with a visor and one red eye, points a finger under a sky of blue rays.
The room closes with the largest drawings in it: a hooded figure holding lights, a bear with glowing goggles, a wolf with a slogan, and a skull mask lit from inside.
Inside a dark frame a hooded, bearded figure with glowing eyes holds out a hand, and round spots of light float around it like bubbles.

A bear sits on a white ground, painted in soft grey and gold, its eyes hidden behind red goggles that glow. Two beams leave the goggles toward the lower left. On its shoulder, almost too small to see, stands a tiny figure. The bear is drawn with long, careful painted strokes, its paws resting on its knees, and the white around it is cloudy, not flat. At 817 recorded strokes, no other work in the room took as much drawing.
A wolf-like creature with tall ears and glowing eyes bares its teeth in the dark, beside the words STILL BULLISH in orange.

A skull mask fills a brown frame, its two eyes glowing yellow like headlamps, a beam falling from them to the lower right. Blue tubes rise from the top of the head, a crown of red zigzag runs under the cheekbone, and a necklace of white beads hangs across the jaw. The ground is a curtain of brown scribble. It is the last of the framed heads, and the one where the eyes and the beam are the same yellow as the paint.

Go back to the bear with its lights on, and then to the bear with its lights off. Everything in the drawing is the same except the eyes, and the whole mood of the creature changes with them. That is what the room is about: a drawn light that decides where you look, and what you can see of the rest.

A drawn border, and inside it one head filling every corner. That is the formula of this room, and it is where the masks of the summer begin. Twenty-three works, two of them from the first winter and the rest from a single month, May 5 to June 3, 2022.

The borders vary: a wavy white and red ribbon, a row of blue stones, a strip of brown, a thin pink line. What they hold is always the same kind of thing, a face made of parts. Eyes are targets, spirals, X marks or lit squares. Teeth come in rows, as blocks, bones or a grille. Between the parts, the square is filled with scribble until nothing is empty.
Follow the X. It arrives on the first work in December 2021 as a cross on a wheel, returns in May on a gold skull, and by the end of the room it is sitting in both eyes of nearly every mask.
Before the mask month there were two framed faces, five months apart. Together they set out the border and the staring eye.

A wavy ribbon of white, red and blue runs around the edge, and inside it a machine of a face is packed with marks: a target eye with a black X across it, pink petals with yellow crosses, a blue wheel with a zigzag rim, and a long mouth of red lines at the bottom. It is the first framed head in the collection, drawn on December 9, 2021, and the X is already there, laid over the eye like a cancellation.
A red frame around a grey field, and a white face with two round staring eyes and a round open mouth, its hair a tangle of white strokes.
May 5 to 7, six works in three days. The border becomes a strip or a row of stones, and the faces turn to skulls, crowds and the first spiral eye.
Behind a border of blue stones on the left and a row of orange tiles below, a purple face with two ringed eyes bares a double row of white teeth.

A gold skull with two red X marks for eyes, a row of grey teeth, and white lines crawling over it like cracks. Around it the ground is black and the border cream, with green and blue stones scattered through both. This is the X at its plainest: two strokes crossed over each eye, drawn in red so that nothing else on the skull competes with them.
A head in profile facing right, with one square eye glowing yellow and a spiral inside it, white bars and yellow fence posts along the left and bottom.
A crowd packed into the frame: a skull with crossed eyes at the lower left, a row of small faces up the right edge, and figures with spiky hair across the top.
One eye a red X, the other a blue spiral, a bone of a nose between them, and a mouth of white blocks, all packed with purple, yellow and orange pattern.
Mid May. The heads turn mechanical, with dials, grilles and lettering, and then on May 25 four masks arrive in one day.
A machine face with a row of six round dials for teeth, each marked with an X, and a beam of light crossing it from the left.
Black and red scribble over a gold figure, the word BULLISH written twice in red, once at the top and once at the bottom.

A mask with one eye a red cross on a yellow target and the other a spiral in a box, a mouth of white teeth in a yellow frame, and a border of pink dots around the whole thing. Blue and magenta scribble fills every space between the parts. The cross is red and the X is gone, but it does the same job: it cancels the eye it sits on.
Two gold cylinders for eyes, each with a red slot, above a grille of white bars and a tangle of orange, black and white scribble.
A mask with a red heart for one eye and a smaller heart for the other, a row of yellow beads under them, and blue tubes across the forehead.
A mask of grey bone teeth, two eyes ringed with scalloped lace, one a planet with a ring and the other a square with a small face inside it, the letters W A G M I along the top.
The last week of May and the first days of June. The X now sits in both eyes, the scribble gets looser, and the room ends with two heads drawn in a single morning.
A head wrapped in white line, its two eyes spirals, held inside a square of black and a border of pink scribbled with gold.
A yellow face with a red X in each boxed eye, a tube for a nose, and a fan of blue rays coming in from the lower right.

A big mask fills the frame to the edges: two eyes with X marks in red and blue boxes, a long mouth of white teeth in a red band, and a crown of red and orange spikes around the top. Pink zigzag runs along the cheeks and the chin. Where the skull of May 6 had a plain red X on gold, this mask puts the X inside a box, surrounds it with pattern, and makes it one part of many.
A dark head with one blue spiral eye and one yellow, lit by a beam from the right, and lilac lines crackling around it like electricity.
A mask of yellow, black and blue with a red X in a round eye on the left and a square eye of zigzags on the right, a row of blue beads around the edge.
A yellow cross in one eye, a red cross in the other, a mouth of grey bars in a red frame, and scribble in blue, orange and white over a dark ground.

A face painted in black, brown and grey, with small pale eyes, a red mouth drawn in a snarl, and lines of red running down the cheeks. Colored scribble in lilac, blue and yellow floats over it without covering it, and there is no border. The mask has become a face again, with a nose, lids and lips, and the X has gone from the eyes. It is the one work in the room with shadow.
Twenty-four minutes later, the same morning, a face in loose line: one eye a red target under a spiky lid, the other a yellow oval, a red mouth with white teeth, inside a thin pink frame.

Look again at the X. On the first work it is one stroke across one eye in a crowd of other marks. On the gold skull it is two plain red lines. By the last week of May it is drawn in both eyes, boxed, colored and surrounded by pattern. Then, on the painted face that ends the room, it is gone, and two small eyes look out instead.

Everything in this room is made of line. Figures are outlines, crowds are tangles, and where a body has color it is scribbled in, not painted. Twenty-three works, beginning with the first drawing in the whole collection on December 8, 2021, and ending with four from the start of June.

The lines change their job as the months go by. In the first week they pile up until a square is full: a crowd of toothy heads, a figure with wings, two black bodies edged in neon. In January they thin out, and a whole scene can be a few white strokes on purple. By June a figure is one black shape with a white edge, standing alone in a grey room.
Count the faces in each one. The room begins with more faces than you can count and ends with a single figure holding a bird.
Six works from December 8 to 12, 2021, including the very first New Nifty on the Block. The square is packed every time.

The first work in the collection: a crowd of heads and raised limbs on cyan, drawn in red, blue, white and yellow scribble over black outline. Teeth are everywhere, in a skull at the top, a grinning head at the left, a jaw at the bottom edge. A hand with spread fingers reaches up at the upper left. Nothing is in front of anything else; the figures share one weave, and a face found in it is lost again as soon as the eye moves.
A green-faced figure with ex eyes sits cross-legged in an orange body with two yellow wings spread behind it, on a ground of white, magenta and black strokes.

Two figures lean together on a pink and orange ground, one with yellow hair, both with round eyes and red mouths, and between them a large red heart. Two smaller hearts float at the sides. The bodies are drawn in green, yellow and white scribble with a thin white edge, and the big heart is outlined in white like a badge. It is the first drawing in the collection with a heart in it, and with 378 recorded strokes the most worked in this room.
Two black figures edged in white and pink stand against a dark ground of colored scribble, one with an X in its eye and the other with a Y, a hand of three pink fingers between them.
One big face: two round red eyes with green X marks, a blue square eye between them, a mouth of white teeth, and thick swirls of red, blue and yellow line around the edge.
Mid December. The figures line up. Seven robed figures in a row, three lumpy ones side by side, a row of ghosts over black grass.
A purple mass with four faces in it, each with a grin of white teeth and small yellow eyes, drawn in white line over an olive grid.

Seven tall figures stand in a row, their bodies long stripes of blue, green, pink and yellow, their round heads burning with orange and red scribble. Each face has two small eyes and a grin. The heads touch a band of fire along the top, so the row seems to stand under one burning roof. It is the first row of figures in the collection, and the tallest.
Three lumpy figures in orange and blue scribble stand side by side on black, each with yellow eyes and a wide grin of white teeth.

Six ghosts hang in a row under a pink sky, their long bodies drawn in thin blue, yellow and white lines that fall like rain, their faces screaming. Black grass stands up along the bottom in white outline. Three days after the row of seven burning heads, the row is back, but the fire has gone out: the heads are pale ovals with dark eyes and open mouths, and the bodies are see-through.
January and February 2022. The lines loosen and multiply, and the figures are harder to find.
A tangle of blue, orange and black line over olive and red, with two grinning heads at the top corners and a white line running around the edge like a frame.

A group of figures drawn in white, green and orange line on purple, their arms raised. One at the center has a dark face and both hands up. Twenty-nine recorded strokes make the whole drawing, and nothing is filled in; the purple shows through every body. It is the sparest crowd in the room, and the first where the line is nearly all that there is.
A figure hangs upside down behind five dark red bars on a red ground, its skull at the bottom with teeth showing, its legs crossed at the top.
A figure in blue, orange and green scribble sits in a chair at a window, on pink, with a second small figure standing on the sill at the upper left.
One week in March. Four drawings that are each a scene or a character, with the line now doing the describing.
A cartoon scene on teal and pink: three smiling faces in a box of yellow dots, a round green tree with a face, a yellow snail with antennae, and pink clouds along the top.
A group of figures in white and yellow line on orange, a grinning monkey at the left and four others with round heads, over a ground of colored bars.
A figure with square glasses and a wide grin crosses its arms, drawn in black, white and green hatching over an orange ground, spikes of hair standing up.
A figure with a huge round head dances with one arm up and one out, drawn in red, white and blue line on dark teal, its face a swirl with a small grin.
After nine weeks, four works from May 30 to June 3. A crowd of yellow characters, then two figures alone in grey rooms, then a pair with red heads.
A crowd of yellow characters with spiky hair on pale blue, the one in front wearing sunglasses and a white tee that says NIFTY INK, pale faces floating behind them.

A black figure in a suit stands in a grey room, drawn with a thin white edge, its head stretched sideways like a balloon with two ex eyes on it. A single yellow flower grows at the lower right. Thirty recorded strokes. In December the black figures were edged in neon and surrounded by scribble; here the same black body stands in nothing at all, and the room is empty except for the flower.

A tall black figure with a white edge stands at the right of a grey room and holds out its arm, and on its hand sits a small purple bird with a yellow beak. The figure's face has two spiral eyes and a row of teeth. A darker square is drawn on the wall behind it. The bird is the one colored thing in the picture, and the whole arm is drawn to carry it.
Two figures with red heads and black hair stand on a yellow ground ruled with white lines, a red heart between them and X marks on their faces, six months after the hearts of December.

Go back to the first work and then to the figure with the bird. Both are made of line. One has more faces than you can count and fills the square to the corners; the other has one face, one arm and one small bird, and most of the square is empty wall. The room is the distance between them.

Two kinds of body share this room. One is a skeleton: a stick figure of bones, drawn in a few colored lines, dancing or walking on a flat ground. The other is a monster: a hunched, furred or armored creature in the dark, with fangs. Twenty works, from New Year's Day 2022 to June 3.

The skeletons are all limbs. Their arms and legs bend at too many joints, their hands are spread like rakes, and their heads are small skulls with teeth. Most of them wear something: a jacket, a tutu, a hat. The monsters are all mass. They crouch, they fill the square, and the light picks out teeth and eyes and leaves the rest in shadow.

The two kinds do not alternate neatly. Watch the stick figures loosen through February, then see the monsters take over the room in April and May, until the last work is a creature hanging in a dark forest.
Three stick figures from the first three days of 2022, then the first monster at the end of the month.

A horned figure in a jacket stands square on an olive ground, drawn in black with a cream fill, its ribs showing through the coat like a fossil. Thin red and yellow lines wander over the whole square in loose rectangles, as if a second drawing had been laid on the first. The hands are two rakes of fingers. The year 2022 begins with this work, made in the morning of January 1.
A stick figure in a pink tutu stands on one leg like a pole, arms out, its head a ball of red scribble with two round eyes.
A lanky figure in blue and orange line dances on teal, one arm raised high in a loop, its small skull grinning with white fangs.

A skeleton painted in dark purple and grey emerges from black, its skull tilted toward you, its ribcage open, one hand held up with the fingers spread. Light catches the top of the skull, the knuckles and the edges of the ribs, and everything else sinks into the ground. It is the first painted body in the room, and the first with no color at all beyond the purple of the bone.
Eight works in three weeks. Skeletons put on hats and cowboy boots, and between them the monsters arrive, one with fangs and one with a grin.

A hunched creature with a long skull, a red mouth of white fangs and two red eyes crouches in grey light, its fur drawn in a halo of black and white scratches. Four days after the purple skeleton, the painted body is back, but furred, with hands planted on the ground and a spine of spikes down its back. The dark around it is not flat; it is made of soft grey discs, like a fog.
Two skeletons in yellow and pink line meet on orange, one bending low and the other reaching down, their skulls grinning with white fangs.
A skeleton in a tall yellow hat stands on teal, its boxy body striped with pink, red and yellow, both arms held out and its ribs drawn in white.
A cowboy skeleton strides to the left on orange, hat tipped, one leg raised, its chest a box of blue and red scribble with a heart in it.
A hunched figure in yellow, pink and blue scribble crouches on olive, its boxy head open at the front with two staring eyes and a row of teeth.
A purple figure with a round head and a wide grin of white teeth holds out its arms in the dark, its eyes two red X marks.
March and April. A moth, a crowned skeleton on a maze, a horned creature, and two more cowboys, one dancing on red and one walking downhill.

A moth with wings of gold and black stripes spreads them across a purple ground, its small red face at the top with two antennae. The body is a stack of striped segments, and the wings are drawn in long curved strokes that follow their shape. Two round tips hang below like feet. It is the one winged creature in the room, and the most carefully built, with 380 recorded strokes.
A horned creature made of colored scribble crouches on all fours in the dark, two round eyes and a mouth of white fangs in its square head.
A cowboy skeleton dances on red, one arm up and one out, white lines of motion curving around it and three white squiggles rising from its hat.
A metallic figure with red ex eyes walks down a black slope on lime green, its body drawn in grey and blue with white highlights.
The last four works, from April 25 to June 3, are all monsters, and all painted. The skeletons are gone.

A blob of a monster fills the square from the black, its mouth a cave of white teeth, its two eyes on stalks with orange lids. The body is drawn in green and brown with scribble over it, and a hand at the upper right holds up a small round thing. In February a purple figure grinned with a row of teeth; here the grin has become the whole body, and the eyes have left the head.
A blue bull with small horns walks through orange fire, its back and legs drawn in blue and green scribble, a bouquet of smoke rising from its tail.
A furry creature with a huge mane of colored strokes grins with white fangs, one red eye showing, on a ground of yellow circles.

A hunched creature with long hair and long thin arms hangs in a dark forest, drawn in black and gold strokes between tall black tree trunks, the sky behind it burning orange. Its face looks down and is barely there. The hands reach toward the ground. It is the last work in the room, made June 3, 2022, and the only one where the monster has a place to be: a forest, with trees and a sky.

Look again at the first skeleton, standing square in its jacket on New Year's Day, and then at the creature hanging in the forest in June. The one is all bone and line on a flat ground. The other is all hair and shadow in a place with trees. The room walked from one to the other in five months.

This room is painted. The marks are soft, broad and blended, and the line, when it appears, sits on top of color instead of making it. Twenty-four works from the first six months of the collection, December 2021 to June 2022, hang here because they share that surface.

What is painted changes from week to week. A dancer and a duck in a room, a sunset over water, a sky of pale cloud, a house in a field, a figure in a yellow raincoat, a woman wrapped in cloth, a rooster, an elephant, a mouse. Between them come color fields with no subject at all: drips, stripes, a plaid of black and red.
In most of the collection the ground is flat color. Here it is air, cloud, light and weather, and the figures stand in it, not on it.
Four works from the first three weeks. Faces float in soft light, a dancer and a duck share a room, and the first color field and the first landscape arrive.

Faces float in pink and gold light, drawn as thin blue and yellow outlines over a ground of soft overlapping discs. Six of them hang at the left and the top like balloons, each with two round eyes and a mouth, and a profile with spiky hair stands in the middle looking right. The whole picture glows, and nothing in it is solid. It was made on December 8, 2021, the same day as the first two works in the collection, and it is the first painted one.

A dancer in a short gold dress raises her arms and shouts, and beside her a duck in a feathered coat stands with its wings folded, under a hooked lamp. Both are painted in gold and brown with scribble over them, and the room behind them is a weave of pink, lilac and gold lines. The dancer's face is red with a wide open mouth; the duck's eyes are narrow and its beak is shut. It is the most peopled painting in the room, with 562 recorded strokes.
No figure at all: vertical drips of orange, red, blue, white and brown run down the square, crossed by a few white and red lines.

A sunset over water. Pale cloud at the top, a band of orange and gold at the horizon, and below it a winding channel of blue water between dark purple and green banks, painted in soft overlapping strokes with scribble on top. It is the first landscape in the collection, made on Christmas Eve 2021, and the most densely drawn work in the room.
January and February 2022. A cloudy sky, a house in a field, and three color fields in a row, then a figure in a raincoat.
A sky of pale cloud, painted in cream, blue and pink discs with yellow light coming through the middle and thin blue and red lines drawn over the clouds.
A house with a pitched roof drawn in brown and lime green line, standing in a field of olive and blue strokes under a sky of blue bars.
On cream: a red block, a white block, a grey ring with a black center, a blue box hanging from a line, a magenta block, and three small green flowers on stems.

A figure in a yellow raincoat with the hood up stands against dark green, its face in shadow under the hood except for a red mouth of pointed teeth and two red marks for eyes. The coat is painted in broad yellow strokes with white lines for the seams. One sleeve ends in a hand drawn in white and red. The figure fills the right half of the square and faces left into the dark.
March and April. A creature in a field of light, trees in a haze, a gown, a wrapped woman, a rooster and an elephant.
A black creature with a striped head and a white grin crouches in a field of gold and purple discs, its spotted tail curling up behind it and a hand reaching out.
Trees in a haze of pale discs, drawn in thin blue, green and white line, a tall trunk at the center and grass at the bottom in loops.
A figure in a huge brown gown turns away on olive, its arms a flurry of orange and black strokes, a spray of colored dots rising from it like confetti.

A woman with black hair in a bun and a small pale face stands wrapped in cloth: blue and pink bands wound across her chest, and a long striped robe of gold, brown and purple falling to the bottom edge. The ground is dark olive and flat. Her mouth is a small red mark and her eyes are two short lines. It is the stillest work in the room, and the only one that looks like a dressed person seen from the front.
A rooster painted in red, purple and blue feathers stands on blue, its yellow beak open, a white belly and a raised crest of spikes.
An elephant with a curled trunk and small round eyes sits on yellow, its hide painted in grey and purple with scribble over it, flames rising from its head and tail.
The last nine works, May 4 to June 4. An angel in the clouds, an astronaut, a mouse, a figure in a hat, a gold armored body, and a barn full of figures.
A creature with a halo kneels in a bank of clouds under a gold sun, its head bowed and its hands raised, painted in brown and gold with white light on the edges.

An astronaut's head inside a round helmet, against black space full of white stars. The face is painted in soft gold and grey discs, with two mismatched eyes, a long nose and a grimace of teeth drawn in orange line. The helmet is a white ring with grey reflections. The face is the most anxious in the room: one eye wide, the other narrowed, the mouth pulled down at the corners.
A mouse with round ears, black button eyes and whiskers hugs its own pink arms on a yellow ground inside a black frame, painted in gold, orange and pink.
A figure in a wide-brimmed hat with flowers on it, seen from the side, its face a blur of pale grey and pink discs against white and blue haze.
A gold armored body with two round yellow eyes and a grin of white teeth stands in a frame, its plates drawn in short strokes of gold, blue and white over black.
A figure with a mass of dark red hair over its face holds a hand to its head, in a yellow shirt on a ground of yellow bars, the face hidden entirely.

Figures hang and climb in the rafters of a barn, painted in brown and gold over a ground of tall vertical strokes. One with a long face hangs from a beam at the right, two more sit on a shelf at the upper right, and a grinning head looks out from the lower corner. The whole picture is made of uprights, beams, legs and falling strokes. It is the last work of New Nifty on the Block's first part, made June 4, 2022.

The first painting has faces floating in pink light, and nothing in it has an edge. The last has figures hanging in a barn made of boards. The soft ground is still there in both. What changed is that the figures found something to hold on to.

A head drawn as a box, with boxes inside it. That is the mask of this room: square eyes holding spirals, targets or crosses, a mouth drawn as a grille of upright bars, and every corner of the square filled with zigzag, beads and scribble. Twenty-four works, from June 8 to August 19, 2022.

The parts are a kit. An eye can be a red X in a box, a spiral in a box, a flower, a planet with a ring. A mouth can be white blocks, a row of fangs, a bar of grey teeth. Beads run along the edges, zigzags run along the brows, and a few tubes stand up on top like hair or a crown. Each mask is a new arrangement of the same parts.

In June the boxes are packed and crowded. In July the masks get a face shape, with a jaw and a crown. In August the boxes become machines and mazes, and the last mask in the room is a long yellow face behind a cage of lines.
The first eight masks, June 8 to 25. Every one is filled edge to edge, and the X and the spiral trade places from eye to eye.

The first mask of the summer: a red X in a yellow box on the left, a purple cross in a box on the right, a band of dark red beads across the brow, and a long white zigzag under them like a row of teeth. Below that, white boxes stand in a row like fence posts. Blue, pink, yellow and black fill every gap. It is drawn on June 8, 2022, four days after the first part of the collection ends, and the whole room is already in it.
A pink mask with a red X in one eye, a ring in the other, a tongue hanging out at the bottom, and a column of brown beads down the right edge.
A pale mask with concentric rings for one eye and a red X for the other, a grid of white teeth, and a row of red flowers down the right.
A dark green head with a red X eye at the right, a row of white fangs, and a stack of blue bars at the lower left, framed in white.

Two square eyes side by side, each a tight spiral, the left orange and the right black and white, in a boxy head with a mouth of zigzag teeth below. Thick white and black lines run around the lower half in right angles, like the wiring of a machine. The ground is red and olive behind the head. It is the clearest statement of the room's formula: the eyes are boxes, the spirals are in the boxes, and everything else is pattern.
A yellow mask with a ringed planet for one eye, a red X for the other, a blue flower between them, and a mouth of white bars.
A grey round head with two yellow spiral eyes and a grin of yellow fangs sits between two figures in black, each with an X on its chest.
Late June to mid July. The box becomes a head with a jaw, teeth get bigger, and crowns of spikes stand up along the top.

A purple ground, and in it a head with a yellow crown, two eyes that are each a mouth of fangs, and below them a wide grille of white teeth in a pink box. The face is drawn in black and white line over orange, blue and green scribble, and purple zigzag runs down the right side. It is the mask with the most teeth in the room: two sets in the eyes and one across the jaw.
A grey head with a crown of orange sun rays, two spiral eyes in yellow boxes, a row of boxes with X marks down the center and a mouth of white fangs at the bottom.
A mask with a flower for one eye and a red X in a spiral for the other, a mouth of yellow loops, and a small face in a box at the lower left.
A blue mask with a spiral in a box on the left and a ringed eye on the right, a bar of white teeth at the bottom, blue and pink scribble filling the face.
A black mask on red with a crown of orange bars, a yellow X in one eye, a ringed eye in the other, and a yellow fence of teeth at the bottom.
A red framed mask with two square eyes, one a spiral in orange and one a spiral in black, a row of white teeth at the lower left and bars of green and blue below.
An olive mask with a red ringed eye and a white ringed eye, a mouth of yellow fangs under a bar of blue, and a grille of white teeth at the bottom.
July 19 to August 19. The boxes turn into machines and mazes, and three of the last four masks are among the most worked drawings in the room.
A red and black head with a crest of white and yellow stripes on top, a grille of blue teeth, and a second mouth of white bars at the bottom.
An olive machine of boxes with a pink spiral in a red box at the upper left, a smaller spiral beside it, and a thick black zigzag running across the middle.

A maze of boxes in red, yellow and blue, with a purple spiral in a dark box at the right, a red curl at the center and a mouth of white blocks at the lower right. Black zigzag runs across the top, pink zigzag runs along the bottom, and a flower sits at the lower left corner. The face has almost disappeared into the pattern; what is left is a spiral where an eye would be and a row of teeth where a mouth would be.
A boxy head turned to the right, with a yellow loop of beads along its jaw, a square eye at the right, and a grille of teeth under a row of orange tiles.

A brown head with a yellow chain of beads around it, a pink box for one eye with a blue ring in it, a flower for the other, and a curling brown mustache over a long grille of white teeth. Three brown legs with white teeth hang below the mouth like a beard. Striped blue and yellow bars stand at the bottom like a collar. With 334 recorded strokes it is one of the two most worked masks in the room, and the only one with a mustache.
A mask with a crown of spikes and two spiral eyes in boxes, one yellow and one white, a row of ringed teeth below and bars of yellow and blue on both sides.

A long yellow face with two pale eyes and a mouth of white and black bars, behind a cage of thin yellow and white lines that cross the whole square. Stripes of pink, red and green stand behind the face, and a crown of white and yellow zigzag sits on its brow. Where the first mask of June packed its boxes to the edges, this one stands back and lets the lines fall over it. It is the last work of the mask summer, drawn August 19, 2022.

In June, the first mask is packed to the edges with boxes, and its eyes are a red X and a purple cross. In August, the last is a long yellow face behind a cage of lines, with two pale eyes that are almost human. The parts never changed. The arrangement did.

The masks in this room are round, or turned sideways. A head drawn as a ring or an oval, with a border of dots or spikes, and the parts arranged inside it: hearts, flowers, spirals and crosses for eyes, and a mouth of teeth that sometimes takes the whole lower half. Twenty-one works, from June 8 to August 19, 2022.

Six of them come from a single day, July 9, when the round mask was found and tried six times in twelve hours. Each of the six has a different pair of eyes. One has a heart pierced by an arrow. One has a flower and a heart together. One has a spiral and a flower. One has an eye like a wheel.
Watch the mouth. In the first mask it is a small open hole with teeth inside. By August it is a jaw of white teeth as wide as the face, and the last mask in the room is a skull with one gold eye.
Before the round masks there were two oval ones, a week apart: a gold head with a spiral eye, and a grey skull with a grin.

A gold head in a frame of dark teal, drawn in loose loops of pink, blue and yellow line over a painted face. One eye is a spiral, the other is a cross in a box, and the mouth is a small open hole with teeth drawn inside it. Two red bars cross the brow. It is the first work of the mask summer, drawn on June 8, 2022, and it still has a painted face under the line, something the later masks let go of.
A grey skull in a grey room, drawn in white and black line with spiky blue lashes, a grin of white teeth and yellow and red bars behind it.
