July 9, 2022. Six round masks in twelve hours, each with a different pair of eyes.

A round mask on blue, with a red heart pierced by an arrow for one eye and a yellow flower for the other, a grille of white teeth in a box below, and a border of zigzag and beads around the edge. The face is filled with blue, red and green scribble, and a green coil sits at the lower left like an ear. It is the first of the six, and the arrow through the heart is the one thing in the room that tells a story.
Half an hour later, a round mask on teal with a red X in a white box for one eye and a black spiral in a red box for the other, a mouth of white fangs below.
A pale blue mask with a border of purple dots, a wheel for one eye, a ringed eye for the other, and a mouth of white bars at the lower right.
A round mask on blue with a red heart for one eye and a lilac flower for the other, a bar of white teeth crossing the lower face, and a border of yellow petals.

An olive mask with a big blue spiral for one eye and a small red flower for the other, a mouth of white fangs in a red box, and a border of yellow spikes with pink and blue beads. Where the morning's first mask had a heart and an arrow, this one has a spiral so large it fills a quarter of the face, and the flower beside it is pushed up into the corner. The eyes do not match in size, color or kind.

A dark oval mask with a flower for one eye and a crossed eye for the other, a grille of white teeth, and a border of blue beads inside a ring of black spikes, on a ground of dark teal scribbled with yellow. The last of the six, twelve hours after the first, and the most worked, with 382 recorded strokes. The border is as busy as the face: beads, spikes, yellow loops and a second ring of blue around all of it.
July 10 to 27. A beam returns, two hearts make a pair of eyes, a mask grows a beak, and the line loosens.
A gold framed head with two glowing eyes, beams pouring from them across the square, a grille of grey teeth and a row of red bars at the bottom.
A yellow mask with two red hearts for eyes, a wide mouth of white teeth in a red box, and a black border drawn in one loose loop.
A magenta mask with a beak like a bird, a ringed eye at the left and a cluster of yellow dots at the right, a mouth of white and yellow bars, and a border of green beads.
A green and yellow mask with a black spiral at the upper left and a round eye with a red band across it, a mouth of red fangs and a second mouth of white teeth below.
A sketchy face on olive, drawn in black, yellow and orange loops, one dark eye at the left and a ringed eye at the right, a pink spiral on the cheek and a mouth of white teeth.
August 11 to 19. The mouth takes over. Six masks with jaws of white teeth as wide as the face, and a skull to end the room.

A round mask on dark blue with a crown of yellow rays, a white flower for one eye and a square with a spiral for the other, and a wide grin of white teeth curving across the lower half. Red zigzag runs down the left side of the grin, and small blue and yellow drops fall beside it. The rays around the edge are drawn as yellow spikes with white beads between them, so the head is a sun.
A big round head with a red target for one eye and a triangle with a blue eye for the other, a jaw of white teeth in a red mouth, drawn in black line over yellow and green.
A mask with a blue spiral eye and a red square eye, a flower at the right, a jaw of white teeth at the left, and a pale blue bar running down across the face like a strap.
A boxy head on red and blue with a green ringed eye and a red ringed eye, a long nose, and a row of white triangle teeth in a black mouth.

A brown round mask with a yellow eye and a green eye, blue bars for a nose, and a jaw of white teeth that takes up the whole lower half, with a yellow zigzag running along the bottom lip. Orange flames stand at the top corners. The head is drawn as one thick black ring over soft brown paint. In June the first mask had a small hole of a mouth with teeth drawn inside; here the mouth is the biggest thing on the face.
A head in profile on red-brown, facing left, with a yellow eye in a box, a black zigzag along the brow, and a mouth of white bars at the lower left.

A grey skull with one eye a ring of teal and one a gold target with spikes, a red beam leaving the gold eye to the right, and a mouth of white and black bars. The skull is drawn in white and black line over grey and gold paint, with purple and blue scribble falling through it. It is the last work of the mask summer, drawn August 19, 2022, a few hours after the last square mask.

The six masks from July 9 were made in one day, and every one of them has a different pair of eyes: a heart and a flower, an X and a spiral, a wheel and a ring. Then look at the brown mask from August, where the mouth has taken over. The eyes were the game in July. By August it was the jaw.

Heads buried in line. In this room the face is drawn, and then drawn over, until it sits inside a tangle of colored scribble like a thing seen through weeds. Most of the grounds are black, slate or brown, and nearly every mouth shows its teeth. Twenty-eight works, from June 16 to August 19, 2022.

Two things happen under the scribble. Some of the heads are painted first, with shadow on the cheek and light on the brow, and the line is laid over paint. Others are nothing but line, and the head is the place where the scribble gets densest. The difference is easy to see once you look for it: paint has edges that are soft, and line has none.
The room's busiest stretch is one week, July 26 to 31, with fourteen heads in six days. Watch the teeth across it. They end up as the one clear thing in a face that has otherwise come apart.
June 16 to July 8. A profile on red, then a run of heads painted in gold and brown with the scribble drawn on top.
A black skull in profile inside a black square on red, drawn in a few yellow and white lines, with a spiral eye, a row of yellow teeth and a stitched line running down the back of the head.

A horned head painted in gold, brown and blue, with heavy lids and a bearded jaw, drawn over in pink, white and blue line. The paint underneath is modelled: the brow catches light, the cheeks fall into shadow, the beard is a block of dark strokes. The line on top loops around the horns and down the face without covering it. It is the first painted head in the room, made June 24, and the one where the paint and the line are most clearly two layers.
A furry monster in the dark with two narrow eyes and a wide open mouth of white teeth, its fur a mass of green, red, blue and white scribble edged in white.
A brown head with a crown of spikes painted in gold, blue and purple, two round ringed eyes and a small zigzag mouth, framed by grey loops.

An elephant's head, or a skull with a trunk, painted in gold and purple with a red target for one eye and a pink spiral for the other, a mouth of white teeth at the bottom of the trunk. Yellow, blue and white scribble runs over the whole head, and purple drips fall from the jaw. The two eyes are the room's two kinds at once: a target on the left and a spiral on the right.
A dark round head in a frame, lit by two gold beams from the upper left, its open mouth a ring of white teeth, painted in brown and gold with scribble over it.
A green head with a grinning mouth of white teeth, two narrow eyes under a dark brow, and a crest of spikes, painted and scribbled on dark green.
Four heads from July 19 to 26. A red X returns to an eye, a brown head wears a bucket, and the line starts to take over.
A dark head with a red X in one eye, a yellow bar across the brow like a headband, and a grille of white teeth, drawn in dense colored scribble.

A brown head on pale blue, painted in purple and tan with a flat top like a bucket, half-closed eyes and a grin of small teeth. Yellow and white dashes ring the head like a string of lights, and purple line loops around it. It is the one head in the room that smiles with its eyes closed, and the only one on a light ground.
A head on purple, painted in brown and red, with one dark eye and one eye of white rings around a red center, a mouth of white teeth, drawn over in blue and white line.
A tangle of dark grey, white and pink line with a small red devil at the right, its spiral eye and grin of white teeth the only clear thing in the picture.
July 26 to 31, fourteen heads. The scribble is densest here, and the teeth are the one clear thing in most of them.

A face in black scribble on orange, with a red X over one eye and a white ring for the other, a yellow bar across the brow, and two rows of white teeth in a dark mouth. The black line is drawn thickest here of any work in the room, in heavy vertical strokes down the cheeks. The X is as big as the eye socket and drawn in red over the black.
A head seen from the side on dark purple, its eye a blue spiral the size of a fist, its mouth a row of white teeth, drawn in orange, blue and black line.
A slate ground, a boxy head drawn in green, orange and white line, a red X over one eye, and a wide grin of white teeth in a red jaw.

A painted head on grey, in brown, black and gold, with two eyes that look out, a flat nose and a closed mouth, drawn over in yellow and purple line. Nothing is bared here. It is the one head in the room with its mouth shut and its eyes open, and the one most like a person. With 296 recorded strokes it is also the most worked.
A bear-like head on brown with two ringed eyes, a red mouth of white teeth at the bottom, and a second row of teeth above it, drawn in dense colored scribble.
A brown figure with a mop of hair, square glasses, a grin of white teeth, and a coat drawn in gold and brown strokes, sitting on a brown ground.
A slate ground, a mask with a spiral eye in a yellow box and a red arrow driving through its mouth of white teeth, drawn in pink, blue and yellow line.

A dark head with a spiral eye at the right and a red X at the left, white teeth in a red mouth, and the yellow bar again, in dense red, blue and white scribble, four days after the heavy black face on orange.
A black skull in profile on red and orange, facing right, with a yellow crown of spikes along the back of the head, a spiral eye, a mouth of white teeth and a yellow bar through the face.
One work from August 19, made the same day as the last masks: a face of spirals in soft gold.

A face made of spirals: a square spiral for one eye, a round spiral for the other, a third spiral at the right edge like an ear, and a mouth of white zigzag. Everything is drawn in thin black and gold line over soft gold circles, and the whole square is a ring of rings. Where the first head in the room was a black skull in a box on red, this one has no edge at all. It is the last work of the mask summer, drawn August 19, 2022, with 57 strokes.

The first skull is flat black in its box on red. The last face is spirals in gold. The one is all edge and the other is all circle. In between, the scribble closed over the faces and the teeth were what was left showing.

Between June 8 and August 19, 2022, nearly every drawing was a mask. This room holds the twenty-one that were not. A figure with a balloon in a city, a man in a cage of red rain, a crow, a valley, a robot in the sun, a dog, a tree, a skeleton by a river. They were drawn in the gaps between the masks, sometimes on the same day.

They do not share a look. Some are a few lines on white. Some are painted. Some are as packed as the masks themselves, and two are crowds of masked figures standing together like a family photograph. What they share is that each one has a place in it: a street, a cage, a field, a fence, a sky.
Look for the horizon. The masks have none; they fill the square. Nearly everything here stands on a line, or under a sky, or beside a wall.
Six works from June 14 to 28. A figure in a patterned field, a figure with a balloon, a figure in ink, a man in a cage, a crow, and a valley.
A red figure with spiral eyes and a grin stands in a field of yellow, green and purple pattern, a small black figure at its feet, white lines looping over everything.

A black figure with a red face and a red chest walks through a pale city holding a red balloon on a long string. The buildings are a few thin lines, a tower, a fence, a window grid, and the sky is patches of blue and pink. The balloon has a small crown drawn on it. Fifty-four recorded strokes make the whole scene, and the figure, drawn in solid black with a thin red edge, is the one dark thing in it.
A figure in black ink on white, seated with one leg out, its head a spiky skull with a grin, drawn in a few thick strokes and thin outlines.

A figure with a crown stands inside a cage of red lines on black, under a roof of yellow and white. The lines fall from the roof like rain, and the figure behind them is drawn in white and yellow line with spiral eyes and a grin, its hands drawn in white at the bottom. Forty-four strokes, nearly all of them the red bars of the cage.
A crow with a red X eye and a red target on its wing stands on a perch in a storm of grey and black scribble, inside a grey frame.

A valley. A blue river runs down between yellow hills, a green ridge rises at the right, and a pale sky of white and blue clouds is drawn over with thin black lines. Everything is scribbled in loops, the hills in yellow, the ridge in green, the river in blue, but the loops follow the land. It is the one open landscape in the mask months, drawn June 28, 2022.
July. A figure with a falling man, a maze of blocks, two crowds of masked figures, a robot in the sun, and a figure in the rain.
A painted figure in purple and gold with a spiral eye looks up at a small figure tumbling in the pink above, drawn in loops of yellow and blue line.
A maze of colored blocks in black, red, blue and green, with yellow beads running through it and a tiny white figure with raised arms at the bottom.

A dark crowd. Masked figures stand together in red, black and gold scribble: a skull with a crown at the left, a round head with a beam at the top, a face with a wide mouth of teeth at the right, and a small figure with a pale face at the bottom. A pink flower sits at the upper left. The figures overlap, and no one has the whole square. It is the first of two crowds in the room, drawn July 10, with 257 strokes.

The second crowd, nine days later. Four masked figures stand in a row, each with blue ringed eyes and a red mouth of white teeth, a black cat with ex eyes beside them and a cat-eared figure at the upper left. The line is white and yellow over black and gold, and the figures are drawn more clearly than in the first crowd: each has a head, a body and a place in the row. Where the first crowd overlapped, this one lines up.
A gold robot with two red ringed eyes and a grille of teeth stands in rays of yellow sun, its body built from boxes, a flower at the upper left.
A figure in a gold hood stands in blue rain under a sun and a band of cloud, a yellow beam crossing it, its face a few dark marks in a glow.
July 31 to August 19. Two flat figures on one day, a skull in a summer shirt, a tree, and the last scenes of the mask months.

A black dog stands on a black hill against pale blue, its mouth open, with short yellow wavy lines in a ring around it. Nothing is inside the black: no eye, no collar. It is the flat silhouette formula from the spring, drawn once more on July 31, 2022, in 49 strokes, in the middle of the mask months.
A figure with a sun for a head walks on black, its body a pink dress and its legs long yellow lines, with a ring of purple discs behind it like a flower.
A yellow skull with blue goggles and a red cap, a grin of grey teeth, in a white tee that says CCO SUMMER, on black scattered with white marks.

A tree in full leaf, painted in hundreds of small dabs of yellow, green, pink and red, standing behind a fence in a yellow light that falls from the upper left. The trunk is a few dark strokes under the mass of leaves, and the grass at the bottom is small dabs too. With 1,758 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the whole collection, and it is the one drawing in the mask months with no face in it at all.
A yellow figure with a long striped neck curls around itself in a field of orange, pink and blue bars, its head at the upper left with a grin of teeth.
A figure with long black hair over a blue body stands on brown, its face a yellow flower with two red ex eyes and a grin of white teeth, small flowers at its feet.
A purple skull with green hair and two red spiral eyes grins on slate, with blue rays around its head and yellow beads at its neck.

A dense scene by a river: two white skeletons stand on a black mound at the upper left, a pink pig with a crown sits at the lower right, a yellow sun with a spiral at the center, and a black bridge with a yellow stripe crosses the top right. Red and blue lines loop over the whole picture. It is the last work of the mask months, drawn August 19, 2022, and the only one in the room with a crowd, a creature, a sun and water all together.

The figure with the balloon walks through a city drawn in a few lines. By the river, everything is packed in at once. Both are places. The masks of the summer have no place at all, and that is why these twenty-one hang together.

Cats, and then creatures. For two weeks at the end of August 2022 nearly every drawing was a cat: black, boxy, big-eared, standing or sitting in a striped room with its teeth showing. Then, in the first days of September, the cats gave way to flat single creatures, each one color on one color. Twenty-six works, August 20 to September 14.

The cats are built the way the masks were, from boxes, rings and grilles, but they have bodies now, and rooms to stand in. Stripes run behind them like wallpaper or a fence. Two of them share one drawing, and that drawing exists twice, published 85 seconds apart, the second time with a signature.
Watch the stroke count fall. The cats are drawn in two to five hundred strokes. The flat creatures that follow them take thirty to fifty. The room ends on a scribbled horse that takes forty.
August 20 to 24. Six cats in five days, from a crowned cat mask to a white cat on yellow.

A black cat mask with a yellow crown sits on a dark red body, on a ground of gold scribbled with yellow bars. One eye is a blue ring with a cross in it, the other a yellow ring with a Z. The mouth is a box of white teeth under a yellow zigzag. It is the first work after the mask summer, drawn on August 20, 2022, and it is both things at once: the last mask and the first cat.
A black cat head with one red spiral eye and one blue, a grin of white teeth, and a crest of green, set in a weave of blue, yellow and black bars.
A cat figure stands with one arm raised in a room of purple and blue stripes, two round yellow eyes with flowers in them, a box of teeth below.

A black cat with two glowing yellow eyes and a wide grille of white teeth fills the square, its ears tall, its chest a black block over a red rug. The eyes are drawn as yellow rings with light inside them, and the teeth are a long bar with black between each one. Stripes of yellow, pink and white stand behind the cat like a curtain. With 395 recorded strokes it is the densest of the first cats.
August 24 to 26. A seated cat in a red room, a white creature in a yellow one, a cat on cream, and a drawing of two cats that was published twice.
A black cat sits upright in a room of blue and red stripes, its face a white loop with a spiral eye, its body ruled with pink lines like a cage.
A white cat with a long neck and a red mouth sits in a yellow room, a small black cat at its feet and a bird on a perch at the upper left.

A black cat stands on a cream ground with a red X over each eye, its ears tipped in pink, a grin of white teeth, and a pink collar around its neck. Its tail rises in a hook. The room behind it is pale: a few blocks of orange, blue and grey, and thin lines running in loops. It is the quietest cat in the room, and the first with the X in both eyes.

Two black cats side by side, the left one with a red X over one eye and a blue ring in the other, the right one with a red X and a green box. A small blue cat sits between them on a shelf. Below them a maze of black boxes with white line, and a yellow spiral at the right edge. The drawing was published on August 25, 2022, without a signature.

The same drawing, published again 85 seconds later, with one addition: the yellow signature at the lower right. Everything else is the same, the two cats, the small blue cat, the maze. Nine more strokes were recorded, and they are the signature. Both were kept, and both hang here.
A cat-eared mask with two ringed eyes full of green and pink line, a cage of white teeth in a red mouth, and yellow beads along the right edge, on pale blue.
August 26 to 28. Two cats drawn in white, a dense scene with a bird, a scribbled cat on cream, and a cat robot in the dark.

A white cat on black, its face a mass of pink, blue and yellow line, with a red X over one eye and a wide open eye on the other side, a blue beam coming in from the left, and a wide grin of white teeth. The ears are tall and striped. Blue and pink beads run down both sides. Its 437 recorded strokes are the most in the room.
A dense scene with a yellow bird on a perch, a rocket, a creature in a green net, a figure with spiky hair at the lower left and a pink face at the right, on black with white crosses.
A black cat robot with a green box eye and a red box eye, a grille of white teeth, and a yellow zigzag running down its side, in the dark.
August 28 to September 2. The drawings empty out. A white coat and a black figure on purple, a brown figure on maroon, and then single creatures in one color on one color.

Two figures on purple: a white coat with a red cap, drawn in a few black lines, and a small black figure with a cloud of curly hair and a yellow eye. Eighty-two recorded strokes. Two days after the white cat on black, with its hundreds of lines, the drawing has emptied out to two shapes and a flat ground.
Two creatures with crowns and red ringed eyes lean on each other on a floor of yellow stripes, in a room of blue stripes, drawn in white, pink and black line.
A dark red figure dances on yellow, one leg raised, its head a long oval with a few yellow stitches, drawn in thirty-one strokes.
A blue creature with a crest of zigzag and a yellow spiral eye walks on dark red, one arm held out, its body striped with the ground color.
A pink creature with a crocodile snout, a target eye and a crest of spikes stands on black with one leg raised, its fur drawn in pink zigzag.
A teal creature drawn in line only, with a crest of zigzag, a red target eye and red teeth, standing on dark grey with its arms hanging.

A black skull in profile on lavender, with an X for an eye and a few purple lines for the jaw and the teeth, ringed with short black wavy lines. A black oval lies below it like a shadow. It is the flat silhouette from the spring, back for one drawing, and the X that sat on the cats' eyes is now the only mark on the face.
Twelve days later, a horse drawn in yellow, orange and white scribble over a black body, walking on teal with its head down and a mane of white lines.

Look again at the first cat, crowned and packed to the edges of the square, and then at the skull in profile, one black shape on lavender. The room moved from hundreds of strokes to a few dozen in two weeks. The X stayed in the eye the whole way.

Heads that look like people. After a summer of masks, the faces in this room have brows, lids, cheeks and worried eyes. They wear hats. Some are painted, some are a single line, and a few are skulls lit by colored beams. Twenty-three works from August 20 to October 5, 2022.

The eyes do the work. A mask's eyes are rings and spirals; these eyes have whites, pupils and lids, and most of them look somewhere. An old man looks past you. A woman with pink hair looks down. A face in blue line looks straight out with tears on its cheeks.

Watch what happens on October 3, when three portraits are drawn in a morning with almost no color, in a single wandering line. After them the room closes with two round heads in goggles, each with words beside it.
August 20 to September 2. A head in black scribble on red, an old man with worried eyes, and a face on yellow with a red target for one eye.
A head drawn in heavy black scribble on red, its face a tangle of pink line, a single yellow bar across the eyes like a blindfold.

An old man's face fills the square, painted in grey, green and yellow with scribble over it, his eyes wide and unmatched, his mouth open on a row of teeth. The brow is furrowed and the cheeks are hollow. Blocks of blue, green, yellow and red stand around him like a wall. It is the first face in the collection that looks frightened, and with 267 recorded strokes one of the most worked in the room.
A head on yellow, painted in grey and green, with a red spiral target for one eye and a red cross for the other, its teeth bared, a striped collar below.
September 6 to 8. Figures lit by beams, a wrapped head in goggles, a man in a bucket hat, a profile in line, and a face under a top hat.
Two dark figures stand against black, each with two glowing yellow eyes, and beams of gold pour from the eyes down to the lower left.
A head wrapped in white bandages on yellow, with two round black goggles and a grin of pointed teeth.

A man in a green bucket hat, painted in pink and brown, with two round glasses over two round eyes and a round open mouth. His neck is thin and his shoulders are lost in a town of blocks and lines in red, blue and black. The hat is drawn in green and black with the brim turned down. He is the first person in the collection to wear a hat and glasses.
A profile in line on dark green: a head with yellow hair, a pink face, one eye looking out, and a blue coat, drawn in thirty-seven strokes.
A red face under a black top hat, with two yellow crowns for eyes, a bar of white teeth and a row of yellow beads across the brow, on dark red.
September 14 to 22. A hatted face with fangs, a scribbled face with teeth, three skulls lit by beams, a gridded face and a woman with pink hair.
A face in a black hat with a spiral eye and a red eye, a mustache, a mouth of fangs, and green dots floating beside it, on a ground of blue stripes.
A painted face in grey and gold with a tangle of colored scribble over it, two round eyes, and a mouth of white teeth in a red frame.

A skull on lavender, painted in purple, green and pink, with a beam of color crossing its eyes from the left, and a row of white teeth at the bottom. One eye socket is filled with grey and red rings; the other is dark. Thin yellow and blue lines wander over the ground. The skull is the one in the room that is almost a face, with a nose and lips drawn in, and the color is the softest.
A skull in grey, green and purple on a ground of soft olive circles, its eyes two dark hollows, a rainbow beam crossing from the left.
A face in black and orange line on tan, its brow ruled like a grid, two round grey eyes, and a mouth of white bars.
A woman with pink hair looks down on tan, her face orange, her eyes two blue rings, her mouth a row of white marks, in a blue coat.

A skull in the dark, painted in black and grey with yellow and red line, two beams coming in from the sides to meet at the eyes, a row of white teeth below. Where the lavender skull was soft and lit from one side, this one is lit from both, and the light is the only color. Black fingers reach up from the bottom edge.
A hatted face with a spiral eye, a mouth of white bars and a beam from the left, in a field of colored rays, drawn in yellow and black line.
A cat-eared face in purple, pink and green with one huge eye and one small, a mouth of fangs, on dark navy.
A face under a black top hat, split into a dark red side and a yellow side, with two eyes of different sizes, a grin of white teeth, and two white-gloved hands below.
October 3, 2022. Three portraits in a single line, drawn in three hours, then two round heads in goggles to close the room.

A face on blue drawn in one black line, with tan patches for the cheeks, two eyes with white tears, a red mouth, and yellow zigzag for the hair. A hand rises at the left. The line wanders from the brow down the nose to the chin without lifting, and the color is laid on in a few flat patches. It is the first of three portraits drawn that morning.
A face on yellow drawn in black and red line, a tear on each cheek, red lips, the hair a loop of orange and black, drawn an hour and twenty minutes later.
A face on olive drawn in yellow, black and red line, a red mouth the only solid mark, drawn in twenty-seven strokes an hour after the second, the sparest of the three.
A round yellow head on black with pink spots on its scalp, blue goggles, a mouth of white bars, and the words GRIFTERS GONNA GRIFT and INKERS GONNA INK written in blue beside it.

A round blue head on black with yellow spikes standing up from its scalp, pink goggles, and a sunburst for a mouth, with INKERS GONNA INK at the lower left. The day after the yellow head, the same shape returns in the opposite colors, with a beam of gold falling from the mouth. It is the last portrait in the collection, drawn October 5, 2022.

Look again at the old man from August, painted in a hundred small strokes with his eyes wide, and then at the face from October 3 drawn in one line with a tear on each cheek. The second has a tenth of the strokes. Both are faces that look at something, and that is what sets this room apart from the masks.

The last masks. Crowned, packed, and drawn in the dense scribble of the summer, these are the faces that ran alongside the cats and the portraits from August 20 to September 17, 2022. Then, after four weeks of silence, three works on October 15 close the collection: the first drawing redrawn, which its title calls a fork; number 300; and the collection piece, number zero zero zero zero. Twenty-one works.

A crown is a zigzag of three or five points on top of the head. It sits on a mask with ex eyes, on a profile with a cigarette, on a winged figure, and on the skull of number zero zero zero zero. The eyes below the crowns are the summer's eyes, crosses and spirals in boxes, and the mouths are grilles of white teeth.
The room ends on the three works made on one day. Watch the first of them: it is the first drawing in the collection, drawn again ten months later, and the room's last word on what changed.
Four masks from the first day of the room, August 20, 2022, all crowned or spiked.
A dense face with two spiral eyes in boxes, a long nose and a small mouth, drawn in red, blue and orange line over stripes of every color.

A purple crown with a yellow zigzag sits on a grey mask whose right eye is a red X over a yellow ring and whose left is a box of bars. The mouth is a grille of white teeth in a red box. The body below is a cage of black and yellow lines on a red block, and green and purple bars stand at the edges. It is the clearest crown in the room, drawn on the first morning.
A mask in profile facing left, with a crown of black spikes, a yellow spiral eye and a long grille of white teeth, on orange scribbled with blue.
A dense mask with a red X in a round eye and a white ring for the other, a bar of blue across the brow, a mouth of white and black bars, on stripes of orange, blue and purple.
August 22 to 29. A crowned orange mask, a robot in white, a yellow face with a nose, and a sun with an X for an eye.
An orange mask with a crest of red spikes, a black spiral eye at the left, a white box eye at the right, and a mouth of white bars, on a ground of yellow and black bars.

A robot figure on white, its head a box with two glowing yellow eyes under spiky lids, a wide red mouth of white teeth, and a body of black and white bars with pink and blue inside. Red paint runs down the sides like spilled ink. It is the one mask in the room with a whole body and a white ground, and with the red at the edges it looks like it is standing in something.
A yellow face with a long nose, one eye a ring and the other a spiral, a bar of red across it, and a mouth of white teeth, on green and yellow bars.

A yellow sun with a face on a red ground: one eye an orange X, the other a black box, a zigzag of white teeth for a mouth, and pale drips running down from the bottom of the sun. Red strokes cross the sun from the left, and two small triangles stand at the bottom like tents. The sun fills most of the square and sits inside a soft white ring, so it glows.
September 4 to 17. Eight masks: dense ones with ex eyes and teeth, a sparse robot on lavender, a profile with a cigarette, a white oval on black, a winged figure, and a profile lit by a beam.
A dense mask with a red X in each boxed eye, a crown of yellow bars on top, a mouth of white teeth in a red box, and yellow ovals all around.
A purple scribble mask with a yellow bar through one eye and a blue cross over the other, two mouths of white teeth, and yellow drips from the top.
A mask with a crown of white spikes, a white ring eye and a red X eye, a mouth of white teeth in a red box, on brown with orange bars.

A robot mask on lavender drawn in a few lines, a red X in a black ring for one eye, a red bar for the other, a box of white and red bars for a mouth, and thin legs below it like a stand. Forty-one recorded strokes. Set beside the purple crowned mask from August, it is the same arrangement with the scribble taken out: the X, the box and the grille, and nothing else.
A blue mask with two crowned eyes, one a ring and one a box, a wide mouth of white teeth in a red frame, and bars of red and orange at the sides.

A profile in pink line on slate, facing right, with a red spiral eye at the left, a cross in a ring at the right, a mouth of white teeth, and a cigarette drawn in white line with smoke at its tip. Blue hair in zigzag runs along the top. Fifty-four strokes. It is the one mask in the room that smokes.
A dense mask with a red target eye and a dark eye, a mouth of yellow teeth in a pink box, a flower at the lower right, on orange and red bars.
A white oval mask on black, filled with fine colored scribble, with two ringed eyes, a dark nose, a small mouth and a red ear at the right.
A winged figure with a yellow head and two red ex eyes spreads black wings over a ground of brown, yellow and purple, a yellow bar across the bottom.
A profile in brown with a beam coming in from the left to a ringed eye, a grille of white teeth, and green and pink line over the face, on brown.
Four weeks after the last mask, three works on one day close the collection.

The first drawing in the collection, drawn again. A crowd of heads and raised limbs on cyan, with teeth at every size and a hand with spread fingers, as in December 2021. The colors are the same. The lines are looser and the figures larger, with a pink face at the center and a dark figure at the upper right. A small round badge sits at the lower left, and the title says fork. It was drawn on October 15, 2022, the first of the three that day.

A skull mask in the dark with a glowing yellow eye and a beam coming in from the left, its mouth a grille of white teeth, blue bars along the top like a crown, and coils of green and purple at the sides. Number three hundred, drawn two hours after the fork. The light is the summer's light, from the beam room in May, falling on the summer's mask.

The collection piece, an edition of one, drawn last on October 15, 2022, four hours after the fork. A purple skull in profile with a red X for an eye and a row of white teeth, under a crown of orange and red bars, with a yellow sun grinning at the upper right. Green bars stand at the left and yellow ones at the right. Everything the collection drew is in it: the crown, the X, the grille, the sun, the beads, the scribble. Nothing else in the room took as many strokes: 448.

The fork of the first drawing and number zero zero zero zero hang side by side at the end. One is the collection's first idea, redrawn. The other is everything the collection learned in ten months, packed into a single skull. Between them is the whole of New Nifty on the Block.

People, painted fast. The Rawblocks series opens with a run of portraits, most of them drawn between November 5 and 9, 2022: a man in a plaid shirt with a cigarette, a hunched man in a cap, a figure in a hooded cloak of polka dots, a man in a beanie and beard. They are painted in soft discs of color with a loose line drawn over them, and the line is what makes them people.

Each one wears something. A cap, a bandana, sunglasses, a fur coat, a hoodie. The clothes are often more worked than the face, and the face is a few strokes: two eyes, a red mouth, a cigarette. The grounds are flat and plain, grey, olive, blue, so the figure is all there is.

The room opens with three cartoon heads from the first night and closes with two painted figures from January 2023. Watch how the painting changes between them, from a round yellow head to a woman in yellow light with no face at all.
October 30 and 31, 2022. Three cartoon heads to begin: a round yellow head in pink glasses, a face in sunglasses in orange rays, and a red-haired head on legs.

A round yellow head wearing pink glasses, with a small red mouth and one curl of hair, on a body in a blue coat holding out a black glove. The ground is teal with soft discs, and a row of yellow triangles stands on the head like a crown of spikes. It is the first Rawblocks work after the two masks of May, drawn October 30, 2022, and it is a cartoon: a circle for a head, a dot for a nose.
A face in dark sunglasses drawn in yellow and purple line over a ground of orange rays, its mouth open on a row of white teeth.
A red-haired head on two black legs walks across orange, grinning with white fangs, one arm out, its hair a cloud of red scribble.
November 5, 2022. Six portraits in two hours, from a man in plaid to a hunched man in a cap.

A man with a red cap of hair and blue eyes stands in a plaid shirt, painted in grey, brown and teal with white line over it, a cigarette at his lips. The ground is brown with dark shapes at the right. The shirt is drawn as a grid of lines over dark paint, and the face is a few strokes: two blue eyes, a red mouth, a line for the nose. The November portraits begin here.
A man in a blue striped shirt sits with his hands on his knees, his trousers black with white stripes, on a grey ground, his small face painted in brown.
A man in a camouflage shirt raises one arm against dark green, his hair blue, his mouth red, drawn in white line over painted tan and brown.

A figure in a hooded cloak of blue and white stripes with yellow polka dots, a brown face inside the hood drawn in orange scribble with one blue eye, on teal inside a loose white frame. The cloak is painted in soft blue with the stripes and dots drawn over it. The face is small and the cloak is huge, and the frame around the whole thing is drawn in a few white strokes, like a window.
A hunched man in a dark cap looks down against purple, his face painted in gold and brown with a red eye, a band of pink light crossing behind him.
November 6 to 8, 2022. Eight portraits: glasses and curly hair, pink sunglasses, a cap and a cigarette, a bandana, a beanie and a beard.
A man with curly hair and glasses in profile on olive, painted in grey and lilac, with red lips and a dark coat, the glasses drawn as a single lens.
A face drawn in black line with curly hair, lit by rainbow rays from behind, its eyes yellow and its mouth a grin of teeth.

A man in pink sunglasses and a blue hood, painted in brown and grey, his hair a crest of red and orange strokes, his mouth open on orange teeth with red drips falling from it. The sunglasses are one pink shape across the face with a dark lens. The hood is blue with white line. With 585 recorded strokes it is one of the most worked drawings in the room, and the drips are the one violent mark in a room of calm faces.

A man in a blue cap and sunglasses with a red beard smokes a cigarette, in profile on olive with a field of white dots behind him. The cap is drawn in blue with a dark brim, the sunglasses are black with a purple lens, and the beard is orange scribble. His jacket is red with white sleeves. The cigarette is drawn in white with a red tip. It is the room's most complete figure: hat, glasses, beard, jacket, cigarette, all in one.

A profile in a red bandana and glasses, with a gold earring drawn as a spiral, red lips, and a yellow jacket, on a ground of soft yellow and pink discs. The bandana is drawn in red scribble with a blue band across it. The face is painted in pink and lilac and drawn over in black. At 708 recorded strokes, no other work in the room took as much drawing.
A painted head with green curly hair and a small red mouth on blue, its face grey and purple with two round eyes, a hand at the shoulder.
The same head, half an hour later, with red goggles and a beam of gold pouring from its mouth to the right.

A man in a red beanie with a brown beard and blue eyes, in a yellow jacket, on blue. The face is painted in dark blue and brown with colored scribble over it, and the eyes are two rings under drawn lashes. The beanie is red with a folded brim. The jacket is yellow with a row of buttons. It is the last of the November portraits, drawn November 8, with 592 recorded strokes.
November 9, 2022, three cartoon heads with horns and goggles. Then, after ten weeks, two painted figures from January 23, 2023.
A cartoon head on red with pink lashes, yellow eyes, pink cheeks, a mustache and a horn, two black hands raised at the sides.
A dark cartoon head on purple with a crown of red dots and white spikes, orange lashes, and a beam of orange light crossing from the left, on a thin neck of bones.
A head with curly yellow hair, blue goggles, a red clown nose and white lips, on red, with green dots on the cheeks and a striped wand at the right.

A woman with dark hair in yellow light, her face a cloud of pale discs with no features but a blue mark and a small red mouth, her hands drawn in black at the lower corners. Sixty-eight strokes. Ten weeks after the man in plaid, the painting has gone soft: the light is the subject, and the face is almost gone.
A figure with purple hair looks up on black, its face painted in gold and green with scribble over it, one arm raised and the other reaching out, drawn in brown line.

The man in plaid with his cigarette was drawn in a few strokes on the first evening of November. The woman in yellow light came in January. Both are people. One is drawn in line over paint. The other is paint with almost no line, and the face has dissolved into the light.

Patterned masks, and then black figures. This room holds two things that look nothing alike and were drawn in the same two weeks of November 2022. First the masks: faces packed with pattern, hearts, hatching, spirals, crowns, drawn over paint until the square is full. Then the figures: flat black shapes on a bright ground, a girl in a dress, a creature on all fours, a man in the rain.

The two earliest works in the room are the two earliest in the whole series, from May 2022, and they are masks too, packed to the frame. The masks that follow in November turn into skulls and sun-faces, and then on November 10 the black figures arrive, three in one evening.
Watch the black. In the masks it is one color among many. In the figures it is the whole body, and everything else, the maze, the sun, the rain, is drawn around it.
May 8 and 9, 2022. The first two Rawblocks works, drawn six months before the rest: two dense masks inside white frames.

A mask packed with pattern inside a white frame: a ringed eye in a box at the left, a spiral eye in a box at the right, a mouth of white bars, and around them columns of beads, zigzags and hatching in red, yellow, blue and green. Nothing is empty. The first Rawblocks work, drawn May 8, 2022, with 387 recorded strokes, the most in the room.
A second mask in a white frame, the next day, with a red target eye in a box, a gold eye in a leaf shape, and a wide mouth of white and red zigzag.
October 30 to November 9, 2022. Ten masks: a crowned face with a red X eye, a green skull, two pink faces with one eye each, a half-sun skull, a skull in red rays, and three on pink.
A mask with a crown of red spikes, a red X over one eye and a cross over the other, a snarl of white teeth, on stripes of yellow and teal.
A round green skull with two ringed eyes, one red and one blue, a crown of purple capsules, and a wide grin of white teeth, drawn over olive.

A face in profile on pink with one huge eye ringed in yellow and pink lashes, a red pupil, blue tubes hanging under it, and a small red mouth. The face is painted in dark red and drawn over in white and pink. A black shadow lies along the bottom. It is the first of a pair: the same face returns an hour later with blue hair.
The same face an hour later, now with a crest of blue hair, a yellow flower in its mouth, and a yellow coat, on the same pink.

A skull split down the middle: the left half painted in soft yellow with a pale eye, the right half a gold sun-face with a spiral eye and a ring of yellow rays. A rope of gold runs down between them. The mouth is a grille of white teeth in a gold box. The ground is a haze of orange and purple discs. Two faces in one skull, one quiet and one burning.

A skull mask in a field of red rays, drawn in white and blue line with a target eye crossed in red at the left and a spiral eye at the right, a grille of white teeth, and a crown of spikes. Bones cross below the jaw. The rays are short red strokes on dark grey, standing out from the skull on every side. Its 576 recorded strokes are the most of any mask in the room.
A patterned mask on pink, drawn in loose loops of white, green, blue and yellow, with two ringed eyes and a mouth of white bars.
A mask on pink with a red crown on a yellow head, a red spiral eye, a wheel eye, a rainbow mouth, and a ring of beads around the face.
A round mask with a crest of orange spikes and a spiral eye stands on a stick body with two blue arms, on brown.
November 10 and 11, 2022. A dark scribbled head, then nine flat black figures in two days: a girl, a creature in a maze, a tube figure, a ghost in a frame, a man in the rain.
A dark head on navy with cat ears, two red-rimmed eyes and a mouth of white teeth, drawn in colored scribble over black.
A black figure with spiky hair and yellow legs bends over in a tangle of yellow, white and pink pipes on pink.

A black figure on all fours in a maze of yellow pipes on green, its spiky head a ball with a red X eye and a grin, and three small black figures standing on its back. The big figure is one flat black shape with round feet. The maze is drawn in thick yellow strokes that fill every gap. The flat black figures begin here, and the small ones on its back are drawn the same way at a tenth of the size.

A girl in a black dress with a white face and a ponytail stands in a teal frame, her hands white, a small red flower at her feet. The face is a white circle with two black eyes and an O mouth. The dress has a row of white buttons. Fifty-four strokes. A grey shadow falls behind her. It is the quietest figure in the room, and the only one with a flower.
A black creature with yellow bands on its arms raises both hands in a teal frame, two white eyes with blue pupils, a grin, and a small black figure standing on its head.

A black head in profile with spiky hair on olive, one white eye, and a white hand raised to its chin, inside a dark frame. Twenty-five strokes. The head is one black shape with a long shadow behind it, and the hand is white so it shows. It is the sparest work in the series.
A patterned mask on pink with goggles, two ringed eyes inside them, a crown of white spikes, and a mouth of white teeth, drawn in yellow and black line.

A black figure with a smiling X-eyed face and a red heart on its chest stands in blue rain under a yellow sun with a face, its arms out, two black hands rising at the bottom corners. Question marks float in clouds at the sides. It is drawn inside a cream frame. Where the girl in the teal frame stood still, this figure stands in weather, and the sun looks down at it with its own face.

Six months separate the first mask, packed to its frame with beads and bars, from the black head in profile with its white hand, drawn in twenty-five strokes. The whole range of the series is between them: everything, and almost nothing.

Heads in a few lines, then heads in a storm of them. This room begins in November 2022 with faces drawn in loose colored line on bright grounds, yellow, orange, magenta, green, and ends in March 2023 with the collection piece. Between them the winter heads arrive: dark, scribbled, with teeth bared.

The line heads are quick. A black loop for the skull, a few colored strokes for the features, the ground doing the rest. The scribbled heads are the opposite: hundreds of strokes piled on a dark face until only the eyes and the teeth show through.
The ground goes dark. It is yellow on November 16. By January it is black, and by February the faces have no ground at all, only scribble.
November 16 and 17, 2022. Four heads in loose line on bright grounds, each drawn in under a day of the last.

A head on yellow drawn in black line, with a red box around the face, one small eye at the left and one white ring at the right, and a grin of white teeth. Grey scribble fills the ground behind it, and a few blue lines run through the face. Sixty-two strokes. The head is a box inside a box, the way the masks were, but drawn in air: nothing is filled, and the yellow comes through everywhere.
A head in profile on orange, drawn in black line with a blue X for an eye, a grin of white and black teeth, and an ear drawn as a spiral.
A head on magenta in black and colored line, two ringed eyes, a crest of black scribble for hair, and a mouth of white teeth in a red box.
A head in profile on green, drawn in a single pink and yellow line, with a red eye and a mouth of white teeth at the right.
November 22 and 23, 2022. Three heads where the scribble comes in: a purple head with yellow hair, an orange cat head, and a head lit by a beam.
A purple head with a crest of yellow strokes for hair, two ringed eyes, and a wide grin of white teeth, in colored scribble on purple.

A cat head on orange, drawn in thick black loops over teal and yellow paint, with two eyes, one a spiral and one a white ring, and a small grin. The ears are two black points. A black shadow spreads under the head like spilled ink. The scribble here is black and heavy, and it covers the face so that the features are found inside it. The dark heads begin here.
A head on purple with spiky hair, two boxed eyes, and a yellow beam pouring from its mouth to the right, drawn in colored scribble over dark paint.
January 18 to February 15, 2023. Eight dark heads in scribble, with teeth bared, and one yellow figure with bones.

A dark head with two mouths of white teeth, one above the other, a red propeller for one eye and a yellow ring for the other, drawn in white, blue and red line over black. A black flower hangs at the upper right. The head is outlined in heavy white, and the two mouths fill the lower half. It is the first of the winter heads, drawn January 18, 2023, and the first with the teeth doubled.
A dark head in yellow, blue and black scribble with a blue X over one eye, a box of teeth where the other should be, and a grin of yellow teeth below.
A dark round head in scribble with one eye a red ring and the other a red oval, a grin of white teeth, and a white line running down the brow.

A tall dark head on brown, two hollow eyes with spiky lids, each with a small ring inside, a long dark nose, and a wide mouth of white teeth in red. The head is drawn in grey and brown scribble with a heavy black edge. Two months after the head on yellow in sixty-two strokes, this is the same head drawn in darkness: a box of a face, two eyes, a grin, with the ground gone black.
A dark head in scribble with a ringed eye and a spiral eye, a mouth open on white teeth and a red tongue, on a ground of colored bars.
A yellow figure in a frame with white bones sticking out of its head and shoulders, one arm raised, drawn in yellow and black line over a grey square.
A dense mask with two green hearts above the eyes, a ringed eye and a crossed eye, a grille of white teeth, on brown.
The last night. Four works between March 14 and 15, 2023, and then the collection piece, drawn last.
Three figures in a frame, a skull, a white skeleton and a pink robot, drawn in colored line over a crowded ground, with a small black figure at the lower right.
A mask with a bird's head for one eye, its beak open on white teeth, a red ringed eye beside it, and a beam of red crossing from the upper right, on blue.
A figure with a sun for a head runs across red, in a blue shirt, one arm raised, drawn in red and white line over soft teal discs.
A round mask split in two, half yellow and half brown, with a ringed eye on each side, a red target for a mouth, in a frame of grey, drawn March 15, 2023.

The collection piece, an edition of one, drawn last on March 15, 2023. A crowd of figures from the series in one square: a black crow at the top, a skull head on a striped body, a yellow sun-face with a grin, a black cat with ex eyes, a blue skull in a ring, a small masked head. Every mark of the series is here, the beams, the X, the crown, the teeth. Where the first work of May 2022 packed a single mask to the frame, this one packs the whole series.

Look again at the head on yellow from November, sixty-two strokes of black line with the ground showing through, and then at the collection piece, where the square is full. The room went from one line to a crowd in four months.

Two landscapes to end the wing. They were painted on March 15, 2023, in the two hours after the collection piece, and they are the last Rawblocks works. There is no head in either one. A sun sets through a stand of trees, and light falls through a forest onto a floor of fallen trunks.

They hang here as a coda, apart from the rooms, because they look like nothing else in the series. The brushwork is the series' brushwork, soft discs of color with scribble and line over them, turned for once on trees and sky.
Both painted on March 15, 2023, the sunset first and the forest half an hour later.

A sunset through trees. A yellow sun blazes at the top with rays of pink, blue and yellow, and under it a stand of red-trunked trees with green crowns stands on a field of gold and orange, ruled with dark lines like a floor. The whole picture is painted in soft discs with scribble over them, and the sun's rays reach every corner. With 831 recorded strokes it is one of the two most worked drawings in the series.

Light through a forest. Tall dark trees stand at the sides and a beam of pale light falls between them onto a clearing, where fallen trunks lie in the foreground painted in brown and red. Soft discs of white and lilac float in the light. Half an hour after the sunset, the light has moved from the sky to the ground, and the picture is dark except where it falls. With 1,061 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the Rawblocks, and the last.
The sun in the first picture is the sun-face of the series without its face. Look at it once more, then at the forest, where the light falls on nothing but trees. That is where the Rawblocks end.

Marks laid side by side until they build a surface. The twenty-five works in this room are bands, bars and washes: stripes of color stacked or crossed, blocks set in rows, grids drawn over soft fields. No faces, no figures. The Abstract series has no per-work dates, so the room follows the title numbers.

Two kinds of mark do most of the work. One is a broad vertical stroke, dragged down the square and left to drip, so that a picture is a row of poles or a curtain of color. The other is a thin straight line, drawn across or diagonally over the strokes, so that the surface becomes a plaid, a ladder or a grid.
Behind nearly every set of bars is a soft field of color, grey, pink, maroon or cream, and the bars sit on it like rain on a window.
The first four numbers. Thick loops inside a square, a speckled field, a plaid of thin lines, and diagonals crossing a blotched ground.

A square of pink and yellow on orange, and inside it thick loops of green and yellow drawn in rectangles, with thin lines of pink, white and purple running over them. The loops circle a dark center like a knot. The ground around the square is flat orange, and the pink inside it is soft and cloudy. It is the first of the Abstract works by number, and the only one in the room with a shape at its center.
A field of speckles in yellow-green, pink, blue and gold, with thin vertical lines rising through it like stems, and a band of magenta across the lower edge.
A plaid of thin blue, green and yellow lines over purple, with thick orange and yellow brush strokes laid across it at the left and lower center, and pink at the right edge.

Diagonal lines in red, green, blue and yellow cross the square from both corners over a ground of soft blotches in teal, grey and pink. A dark hairy cross sits at the upper left, and bunches of orange, blue and navy strokes lie scattered over the lines. It is the room's busiest surface, with four layers: the blotches, the thin diagonals, the thick strokes, and the hairy marks on top.
Numbers six to sixteen. Vertical strokes dragged down the square, soft washes behind them, and grids and bars drawn over.
Dense colored dabs in blue, magenta, yellow and green, with dark bristly streaks running down through them like trunks.
Black lace of scribble over soft pink, yellow, mauve and olive, with thin horizontal lines through it.

Pale vertical bars in grey, tan and lilac, washed thin, with a band of orange and black across the middle like a railing seen through fog. The bars drip at their lower ends. Two dark poles stand at the left and the center, and a few thin lines are scratched into the wash at the upper right. It is the quietest picture in the room, and the first where the wash is the subject.
Grey-blue bands washed over a dark ground, with small red and blue squares set along them like lights, and a pale bar at the upper right.
A green and beige wash ruled with thin lines into a grid, orange drips running down from the top, and turquoise at the corners.
Pink and grey vertical bands with a maroon stripe and a dark blue one, washed and splattered, with a pale blue block at the lower right.
Pale translucent blocks stand on maroon like windows, with yellow horizontal lines drawn across them, dashed and broken.

A patchwork of soft color: turquoise, orange, red, purple and yellow blocks laid side by side and overlapping, each one translucent, with darker drips falling through them. There is no line at all. The blocks are soft at every edge, and the color builds up where they cross, so the picture is deepest at the center and palest at the edges.
Pastel brush blocks in pink, yellow, lilac and olive with a purple band across the middle and white strokes laid over them.
Numbers twenty-five to thirty-four. Dark grounds with bright vertical bars, a pale one with rungs, and plaids of stripes and dabs.
A soft patchwork of yellow, mauve, orange and green with black and white line scratched over it in loops and ladders.

Dark ground, and across it vertical bars of red, magenta and cyan, with a horizontal band of cyan near the bottom making a cross. The bars are brushy and bright against the dark, and they drip. A patch of pale pink hangs at the upper left like a lantern. It is the strongest contrast in the room, light bars on a near-black field.
Dark ground with vertical streaks of green, magenta, blue and yellow, a black column at the center, and a hatched band of fine lines along the bottom.
Pale grey bars washed down the square, with black rungs drawn across the right half like a ladder, and teal, red and yellow bars among the grey.

A cream ground, and on it a red circle at the lower left, blocks of yellow, blue, purple and grey, and thin black lines drawn across in a loose grid. A second circle at the upper right is drawn in line with a yellow half. The red circle is the one large shape in the room, and everything else on the page is arranged around it.
Red horizontal stripes on a pink ground, crossed by vertical bars of teal, yellow and grey, with black scratches over them.
On dark olive, yellow bars and squares with a diagonal yellow band across the lower half, pink dashes in a row across the middle, and fine lines like string.
Dense bars in red, teal and yellow, with rows of pink dots and white line scribbled over them in loops.
Two to end the room: a black grid with splatter, and a near-empty cream page with a few shapes on it.

A grey ground ruled with thick black lines into a grid, and across the grid, splatter: black bursts at the upper left and lower right, and bars of red, blue and yellow set between the lines. Where the diagonals of number four made a net of thin lines, here the lines are thick, straight and few, and the marks sit inside the cells.

A cream page with a few shapes on it: a pink block at the left, a green block at the lower right, a red blob and a yellow blob at the top, a grey smudge, and thin black lines drawn in a loose frame around them. Most of the page is empty. It is the sparest work in the series, and the room ends on it.

The plaid of thin lines near the start of the room and the cream page at the end, with its few blocks, were ruled by the same hand. One fills the square with lines until it is cloth. The other draws a frame and leaves the page bare.

Marks thrown, dripped, scribbled and spun. The twenty-seven works in this room are the Abstract series at its loosest: splashes on a bare ground, crowds of short strokes, swirls that turn in a circle, lines that sweep across the square and leave. The room ends on the collection piece, number zero zero zero zero.

Three kinds of gesture hang here. The splash, which hits the ground and spreads. The scribble, which covers it. And the swirl, which turns the whole square into one motion, like a ball of yarn or a storm seen from above.
Look for the one face. Number thirty-eight is a skull drawn in loose loops over soft color, and it is the only face in the Abstract series. It hangs among the swirls because the loops are the same.
Numbers five to twenty. Dots and splashes on dark or grey grounds, with lines scratched through them.

Dots of yellow, pink and cyan scattered over a dark marbled field, with white brush strokes dragged across the middle and bursts of pale yellow like fireworks. The field itself is streaked in green, blue and red, and the dots sit on top of it in drifts. It is the first gesture work by number, and it already has all three kinds: the splash, the scribble in the field, and the sweep of the white strokes.
Red hatching in bunches over grey and green, with cyan and yellow line looping across it, and white hatching at the left.
Bright splashes of orange, blue, magenta and green on grey, with vertical dark streaks behind them and white bursts at the center.
A teal ground with pink and yellow lines scribbled across it, maroon splashes at the corners, and a white patch at the lower left.

A dark brown ground with a tangle of white line at the center, like a figure or a plant, and splashes of pink, yellow and red thrown around it. The white tangle is drawn in loops that climb from the bottom to the top. The splashes are soft and bright. It is the darkest ground in the room, and the one where the splash reads most like something thrown.
Pink and cyan scratches over a soft blue and pink ground, with yellow strokes and black dashes, and a small figure at the lower right.
Numbers twenty-one to twenty-seven. The square fills with short strokes until it is a crowd.
A dense crowd of short strokes in pink, teal, yellow and red, crossing in every direction, with rows of dots through them.
Dark ground with colored bars crossing it: yellow and purple vertical, white and grey diagonal, and tangles of fine line between them.

A brown ground filled edge to edge with short bars of color: red, yellow, cyan, pink, green and white, laid in a loose grid so that they read as a crowd of small flags. Black bars run among them. It is the brightest surface in the series and the most even, with no center and no empty corner.
A textured mass of mauve, green, orange and yellow, drawn in fine scribble, with a block of pink at the lower left and black marks at the center.
Numbers thirty-five to forty. Strokes that turn in a circle, and in the middle of them the one face in the series.
A grey haze with white and yellow strokes laid over it, a chain of dots running down the center, and black marks at the corners.
Dense colored scribble in pink, yellow, green and blue, with spirals drawn in it and black loops over everything.

A swirl on blue: thick black and white strokes turn in a circle around a center of red and gold, with yellow and purple strokes caught in the turn. The black strokes are the longest marks in the series, curving from the top to the bottom edge. The whole picture moves in one direction, like water going down a drain.

A skull drawn in loose black loops over soft patches of red, green, blue and pink on white: two red eyes, a long nose, a row of teeth along the bottom. Thin black lines frame it. It is the only face in the Abstract series, and it hangs here because the loops that draw it are the loops of the swirls around it.
A brown mass hangs over a fire of red and orange strokes on grey, like smoke rising from flame.
Numbers forty-one to fifty, then the work titled pos, and the collection piece to end the wing.

A field of grass-like strokes in blue, grey, white and yellow-green, standing up from the lower edge and leaning to the right, on white. The strokes are thin and close, like reeds. Blue is strongest at the left, green at the bottom. It is the one work in the room drawn entirely in vertical strokes, and the one that most looks like a place.
On maroon, two crossed bars of gold and black at the center like a kite, with splashes of pink, teal and yellow around them.
On teal, splatter and drips in yellow, white, black and purple, with thin orange lines crossing the square.
Round dark blots on ochre, six of them, each drawn in circling strokes of teal and black like a thumbprint.

A swirl of yellow, black and grey-blue on grey, turning in a loose circle like a ball of yarn, with black dots caught in it. The strokes are short and curved, and they follow the turn. The grey ground shows all around. It is the lightest of the swirls, and the one with the clearest circle.
Bright swirling strokes in magenta, yellow, cyan and black on grey, with a magenta loop at the center and white at the edges.
A soft pink and lilac haze with a single thin dark line drawn through it in a wandering path, down the right and across the bottom.
On yellow and white, a splash of black and color at the center dripping downward, with pink, green and purple caught in it.

A round mass of red, orange, teal and brown strokes on grey, drawn in circling layers like a burning ball, with drips running down from its lower edge. The strokes turn around a center and pile up until the mass is almost solid. The grey ground is scratched with grey lines. Its title is pos, the one Abstract work without a number.

The collection piece, an edition of one. Yellow-green and magenta patches on a pale ground, black splatter thrown over them, and a tangle of thin orange, cyan and black lines drawn through the lower half, with a block of black scribble at the bottom. Loops, splashes and lines together. Where the first splash in this room threw dots on a dark field, this one throws its marks over a pale page and draws through them.

Look again at the first splash, dots on a dark field, and then at the collection piece, where splatter, patches and lines are all on one page. The room's three gestures end up together. The swirls between them are the series turning in place.

Pieces made for a moment. The works in this room were drawn for occasions: the hundredth, two hundredth, three hundredth and five hundredth inks, a summer, a pizza day, a greeting. With them hang the few full figures and painted scenes from outside the named series. Twenty-two works, from October 2021 to December 2024.

Most of them carry words. NIFTY INK on a tee shirt, WAGMI on a bottle, a number held up like a sign, slogans written across a face. The words are drawn, not typed, and they sit in the picture like any other mark.
Watch the sun-head. It appears in May 2022 as a figure with a sun for a face, in a tee shirt, on a beach, in the dark, dancing. Two years later it comes back as a pizza.
October 20, 2021, the first day of n n x y z on Nifty Ink: a figure in a cap and a river landscape. Then, in December, a dragon on the water.

A figure in a blue cap and a yellow shirt, drawn in orange and white hatching with the letters N N X Y Z written in pink across its face, grinning with white teeth. The ground is a dense weave of red, green and blue hatching. The first n n x y z work on Nifty Ink, drawn October 20, 2021, and the name is already on the face.

A river runs through a green valley under a sky of pink and white cloud, with a tree at the left and a stump at the right, all painted in soft strokes and scribble. Drawn six hours after the figure in the cap, on the same first day. It is a landscape without a face in it, and with 737 recorded strokes one of the most worked drawings in the wing.

A dragon rises from blue water, its head at the right, its body a long curve of gold and white strokes, its tail trailing across the dark sky. The water is a mass of cyan and white scribble like foam. The sky is black. It is the most densely drawn work in the whole collection, and the only dragon.
January to November 2022. Four milestone drawings for the hundredth, two hundredth, three hundredth and five hundredth inks, and three summer figures with a sun for a head.

Three cartoon characters in green, blue and pink stand in a row with the letters X, Y and Z on their chests and the number 100 drawn above them in pale balloon letters. Their eyes are wide, their mouths open, and they drip at the feet into a grey floor. The milestone for the hundredth ink, made January 28, 2022.
Figures glow in a burst of light, drawn in gold and grey with a hand raised, and the words 200 NIFTY INK at the upper left.

A figure with a sun for a head stands on blue in a white tee that says NIFTY INK, black shorts and sunglasses with X Y Z on the lenses, holding a bottle labeled WAGMI with bubbles rising from it. The sun is yellow with short rays. The arms and legs are yellow lines. The first of three summer figures, drawn May 10, 2022.
The same sun-headed figure at night, glowing in a ring of yellow on black, its tee grey, its arms out.
The sun-headed figure dances on teal in headphones, one leg kicked out, the word WAGMI floating around it with music notes and wavy lines.
A figure in black and white line with a visor and a grin holds a line that runs up to the signature, and a small figure at its feet holds up a sign that says 300.

A face in dense colored line on orange: a long nose, two glasses-like rings, dark hair falling at the sides, a small closed mouth, drawn in black, yellow, blue, white and red strokes over a painted face. It is the milestone for the five hundredth ink, drawn November 12, 2022, and it is a portrait, not a cartoon.
Six numbered works from November 2023 to March 2024 that are figures, not masks: a dancing girl, a rabbit, a hooded figure, a crouching creature, a pair, and a creature with hearts.
A girl with orange curly hair and pink cheeks dances in a teal frame, her arms drawn in blue loops, a shower of yellow and blue dots falling at the left.

On pink, a black figure walks at the left, a red rabbit stands at the center with ringed eyes, and a dark figure with a white smile stands at the right under a yellow sun with a face. Yellow bars float behind them. The three figures are drawn in different ways, the first in black with a yellow face, the rabbit in red scribble, the third in black with a tangle of yellow line. It is the one crowd scene in the room.
A hooded figure painted in dark brown against orange and gold, its face lost in the hood, thin lines ruled across the whole square.
A black creature with a crown of spikes and a grin of teeth crouches on yellow, drawn in black and blue scribble, hatched lines at the right.
Two figures on teal, one in a cap and one with red ex eyes and a red beam, drawn in dark scribble with white line over them.

A green and red creature in sunglasses with a mouth of teeth stands on purple, with three red hearts beside it, each with a small face, and a dark figure in a cap on a pole at the right. A sad sun looks down from the top. Blue raindrops fall. The hearts have faces, the sun has a face, and the creature has sunglasses: everything in the picture looks at something.
May to December 2024. Three pizza drawings in two days, a pink head, and two masks covered in words.

A pizza slice for a head, with red glasses and a grin, under a yellow sun with a face, drawn in orange and gold hatching with yellow rays over everything. Two years after the sun-headed summer figures, the sun is back, and the figure under it has become a slice of pizza. The first of three pizza drawings, made May 19, 2024.
A round head on black with pizza slices on top like a crown, blue glasses, a grin of white teeth, and a slice of pizza on its white shirt.
A man in red glasses and a red cape stands in blue rain holding up a sign with hearts, a pizza flying at the upper right and a small creature at his feet.

A face inside a black frame, covered in words: DIGITAL ART in pink, BLUE CHIP in blue, OG, and a line about going from dishwasher to memewasher along the top. The face has a red crossed eye, a grin of white teeth and a yellow hook of a nose. Green and blue scribble fills the rest. The words are drawn in as many hands as colors.

A mask with a pink flower for an eye and a grin of teeth, under the words NO NEED FOR A WALL in yellow and black, with memewasher, artfluencer and sold by Christies written around it in white, pink and red. Drawn the day after the framed face, December 5, 2024. It is the last work in the collection by date, and it is mostly writing.

A related item from the Scrimshaw collection: the letters G and M drawn in looping colored line on a muddy ground, a greeting by the artist Scrimshaw, dated November 2021. It hangs here with the occasion pieces because it is one.

Look again at the first figure, with the artist's name written across its face in October 2021, and then at the last, a mask under a slogan in December 2024. Three years apart, and both are faces made partly of words.

The masks of 2023 and 2024. After the named series ended, n n x y z kept drawing heads, and these twenty-three are the numbered ones: packed faces with teeth, crowns and crossed eyes, drawn between July 2023 and May 2024. They are denser than the earlier masks, and the line is heavier.

Most of them have a beam. A bar of yellow or red crosses the face at eye height, or shoots from one eye to the edge. Under it the face is built the old way, from boxes and rings and a grille of teeth, but the scribble over it is now thick enough to be a surface of its own.
The ground changes under the masks. In the first it is white or grey. By December 2023 it is green, purple and gold, and the last masks of spring 2024 stand on red, blue and orange.
July and August 2023. Four heads to begin: a dark head in glasses on white, two crowned masks, a round scribbled head, and a skull on stripes.

A dark head in round glasses on white, its skull a weave of colored scribble, a grin of white teeth across the whole jaw, and a yellow beam crossing behind the glasses. The glasses are two yellow lenses in dark rings. The teeth are drawn large, each one outlined, in a row that runs past the edges of the face. The first numbered mask, from July 18, 2023, with 423 recorded strokes.
Two masks side by side in red, black and yellow scribble, the left one crowned, with a red X over one eye and a grin of white teeth, the right one smaller with a box of teeth.
A round head in dense yellow, green and blue scribble on grey, with a ringed eye at the left, a box eye at the right, and a mouth of white teeth in a red box, a yellow bar across the top.
A skull mask on red and pink stripes, drawn in blue, orange and white line, with a target eye, a grille of white teeth and a red heart at the lower right.
November 2023. A patterned boxy mask with hearts, a brown one with red crosses, a white-outlined head with its tongue out, and a dark mask lit by a beam.

A boxy mask on grey, packed with pattern: a red X eye, a box eye, a grille of teeth, two red hearts at the lower center, a cup at the left, and a second small face at the upper left with its own grin. Blue, red and yellow line runs over the whole in loops and ladders. It is the busiest mask in the room, drawn November 2, 2023, with 225 strokes.
A brown boxy mask with two red crosses in its eyes and a mouth of white and black bars, drawn in black and blue line on brown, with a pink flower at the top.

A head outlined in thick white on black, its face a mass of colored scribble, with two red star eyes, a red mouth open on white teeth and a long red tongue hanging out. The outline is one heavy white loop around the whole head and shoulders. The tongue is the brightest thing in the picture. It is the one mask in the room with its mouth open wide.
A dark mask on yellow and olive, with a yellow crossed eye at the right, a beam of orange shooting from it, a grid of lines over everything and a red mouth of white bars.
December 28 to 30, 2023. Eight masks in three days: rays, a crown, a flower eye, a pink hand, a yellow cap, small skulls, red hands, and a head in beams.
A mask in a field of yellow and orange rays, with two ringed eyes, a grin of white teeth in a red mouth, and purple strokes like lashes.
A mask on purple outlined in thick white with a scalloped edge, a crown of white spikes, a box eye, a bar across the brow, and a grille of white teeth in red.

A dark mask on green with a crest of black spikes, a blue flower for one eye and a box with a ring for the other, a red beam from the left, and a grin of white teeth. Rows of red hearts run down the right edge. The flower eye is drawn with pointed blue petals around a yellow center. It is the first of eight masks drawn in three days at the end of December 2023.
A dark mask on purple with a pink hand pressed to the top of its head, two ringed eyes, and a grin of white teeth in a red mouth, yellow line around.
A head in a yellow cap on grey, its face a cage of white and red line with two ringed eyes and a grin of white teeth, in seventy-two strokes.

A grey skull mask with a pink hand and a crossed eye at the left, a box of teeth in red, and five small white skulls floating at the right, each with its own face. A red beam crosses from the left. The small skulls are drawn in black line on white, like a crowd of ghosts watching. It is the one mask with company.
A mask with a red crossed eye and a spiral eye, a grin of white teeth, and two red hands raised at the bottom corners, on dark blue.
